a547eac4-472d-532a-8452-486859f4e916.name: Parish Church of Our Lady of the Snow
a547eac4-472d-532a-8452-486859f4e916.description:
A network of elongated *rocaille* scrolls and cartouches, into which floral twigs and garlands are interwoven covers the walls of the church like lace to form a framework for the wall paintings. Due to the long construction period, the stucco decoration was created over a long period, but nonetheless is based on an extensive, uniform iconographic programme. The Marian topics include the *Legend of Our Lady of the Snow* and the *Foundation of the Roman Church of Santa Maria Maggiore* shown in a number of scenes in the sanctuary of the church (transposed into one of them is a contemporary depiction of the foundation of the church in Kutina). Considerable space on the walls and ceiling of the nave is devoted to the *Passion*. Accompanying these is a sequence of emblematic depictions based on the Old Testament as well as motifs relating to the Mysteries of the Joyful, Sorrowful and Glorious Rosaries.  
Authorship of the wall paintings has not been thoroughly elucidated yet, partly because in the forms the personal styles of three painters can be observed, while the only signatures to be identified are those of Franciscus Weitenhiller of 1776, and Joann Joseph Görner (probably a Varaždin painter) of 1779. While Görner painted the ceiling paintings in the nave, Franciscus Weitenhiller painted the figurative images on the walls of the sanctuary and nave (many of which were subsequently heavily retouched) integrated in the "lace" of the *rocaille* stuccowork. Because of the misspelled signature, the author was at first identified as Josep Weitenhiller (who it is recorded worked in Slovenia). There are also some excellent woodcarvings. The High altar (1739) is attributed stylistically to the Zagreb sculptor, Joseph Weinacht. Weinacht was one of the most accomplished local sculptors of the first half of the 18th century whose style shows the influence of contemporary Styrian sculpture, which suggests that he trained there. The pulpit (around 1761) is ascribed to the Zagreb sculptor, Franjo or Franz Straub (1726–before 1771), and is classified as among the most luxurious and opulent Baroque embodiments in north-west Croatia, as well as an outstanding specimen of dynamism aspiring towards the monumental, characteristics that define his work.
a547eac4-472d-532a-8452-486859f4e916.short_description: A church with a nave only and no aisles, it has a belfry on the facade and is surrounded by a covered walkway. The simplicity of the exterior is much at odds with the rich interior, which is among the most luxuriously fitted-out Baroque churches of northern Croatia. The integrity of the opulent Baroque interior is achieved above all through the rich stucco decoration that covers the walls like lacework, framing the wall paintings dedicated to Marian and Christological subjects.
a547eac4-472d-532a-8452-486859f4e916.dates: High altar: 1739; pulpit: c. 1761; stucco work and wall painting: 1765–1779
a547eac4-472d-532a-8452-486859f4e916.method_for_datation: Archival documents and inscriptions on the monument.

a547eac4-472d-532a-8452-486859f4e916.history: The Baroque church was built on the site of an older building. Construction took a long 40 years, with the sanctuary completed in 1729; the nave in 1748 and building concluded in 1769. Count Karlo Erdödy II and his wife, Countess Erdödy, financed the construction and fitting-out of the church from 1740.

a9e17673-d137-5b5c-89ad-8c71949fda7f.name: *Maria Varasdiniensis*
a9e17673-d137-5b5c-89ad-8c71949fda7f.description:
The figures of the Virgin Mary and Child Jesus are hieratically positioned front-on. Beneath a textile canopy edged with labrequin, the ends of the drapes lifted and knotted, both wear conical cloaks, white wigs and crowns. At the top of the canopy is a gold ring with rays, upon which is the dove of the Holy Spirit with outspread wings. The ornamentation on the cloaks of both Mary and Jesus are motifs from the beginning of the 18th century, mostly acanthus and other foliate scrolls. In the middle of each of their cloaks is a painted gold heart within which are their individual monograms. On the other hand, the faces and wigs of both Mary and Jesus already show Rococo characteristics.  
The representation of Mary and Jesus in conical cloaks is a votive scene that first appeared during the Baroque period. More usually stiff cloaks scattered with floral motifs and adorned with jewellery such as chains and pendants hang over the cloaks like garlands.  
One of the foremost characteristics of the Pauline order was its veneration of the Blessed Virgin Mary, which resulted in her central place in their iconography. In 1672 there were 80 churches dedicated to the Virgin Mary.  
This votive painting of Mary, which hung above the pulpit in the nave of Lepoglava church, was probably intended for Varaždin as the Virgin Mary was its patron.
a9e17673-d137-5b5c-89ad-8c71949fda7f.short_description:
A crowned Mary and Child Jesus stand front-on under a textile canopy. They both wear white wigs and conical cloaks richly decorated with gold hearts within which are their monograms. This votive-type Virgin and Child first appeared during the Baroque period.  
The Pauline Order especially revered the cult of the Blessed Virgin Mary and her portrayal had a central place in their iconography.
a9e17673-d137-5b5c-89ad-8c71949fda7f.holder: Diocese Museum of the Zagreb Archdiocese
a9e17673-d137-5b5c-89ad-8c71949fda7f.obtention: The painting came from the former Pauline Church in Lepoglava, Hrvatsko zagorje and gifted to the Diocesan Museum in Zagreb in 1940.

keywords: Lepoglava; Pauline Order; conical Madonna; floral decoration; vegetal decoration; jewellery; zoomorphic imagery; Christian themes

a9e83744-68da-5616-9775-18e9d9b4eb46.name: Svatý Kopeček (“Holy Hill”)
a9e83744-68da-5616-9775-18e9d9b4eb46.alternate_name: Basilica of the Annunciation at Svatý Kopecek – Basilica Minor
a9e83744-68da-5616-9775-18e9d9b4eb46.description: The church frontage, with wings for the two residences, lies at the top of a hill rising abruptly over the Olomouc flatlands and dominating the surrounding landscape. The segmented, three-axis frontage of the church protrudes into the surrounding space. The portal is crowned with statues of Generosity, Glory and Hope by J. Winterhalder Sr. (1731); the niches contain statues of St. Stephen (patron saint of the Hradisko Monastery), Sts Augustine and Norbert, patron saints of the Premonstratensian order, and the Virgin Mary of Svatý Kopeček with Child, in the upper section. The residential wings are lined with statues of the Apostles and two Protectors from the Plague. The church vault is covered with organically interconnected stuccos and frescos. In the window lunettes, the Four Ages of Man sing praises to the Virgin Mary. Two oval frescos depict Mary’s Devotion to God and Mary as Protectoress from the Onset of the Devil. The south wing houses several historical halls, such as the Chinese Hall and the festive Andrýsek Hall, with pictures by P. Troger. Behind the church complex are an open semi-circular cloister and a chapel, making up a spacious courtyard.
a9e83744-68da-5616-9775-18e9d9b4eb46.short_description: With a spatially segmented frontage opening onto the countryside, the pilgrimage complex is a typical example of Counter-Reformation architecture. The church vaulting, decorated with spectacular stuccos, is among the largest specimens of the style north of the Alps. The vaulting was created by Italian sculptors and decorators, whose further work had a profound influence on art in Moravia. The complex, equipped by leading artists from Vienna and Olomouc, includes a unique series of artworks from the second-half of 17th century, only a tiny proportion of which have survived in the Czech lands.
a9e83744-68da-5616-9775-18e9d9b4eb46.method_for_datation: Handke’s painting is dated. A print of the high altar, created on the occasion of the coronation of the Marian picture in 1733, gives Fontana as the (concept) artist. Archive sources regarding the building such as contracts, receipts and a chronicle of the Premonstratensian residence have survived.

a9e83744-68da-5616-9775-18e9d9b4eb46.history: Legend has it that the chapel on the hill was built by Andrýsek, an Olomouc burgher who had a vision of the Virgin Mary. In 1645 the chapel was plundered by the Swedish army. The abbot of the Premonstratensian Monastery in Hradisko asked Bishop Karel II of Lichtenstein for permission to build a new Church of the Annunciation. In 1684, two single-floor residences were added to the sides of the church, the one on the north for priests and that on the south reception halls. The pilgrimage site was visited by Empress Maria Theresa (1748). In 1784 the church was granted the status of “basilica minor”, meaning that pilgrims could receive the same indulgences there as in Sta. Maria Maggiore, Rome.

af7b7b45-598f-5e3c-8472-5d1ad570467e.name: *The Immaculate Conception with the Saints Petronius and Dionysius*
af7b7b45-598f-5e3c-8472-5d1ad570467e.description:
This altarpiece is one of the most celebrated works of the young Giovanni Antonio Burrini. It was commissioned by the noble Ratta family at the end of the seventeenth-century. Two saints are surrounding the Virgin. They are Petronius the bishop and patron of Bologna, and Dionysius the martyr and bishop of Paris who is often confused with the Areopagite. Saint Dionysius was probably painted by request of the patrons. It is believed that one of the members of the Ratta family was a diplomat sent by the pope to France to persuade Louis XIV to abolish the edit of Nantes and restart the prosecution of the Huguenots.  
The altarpiece is built on a pyramidal composition and is dedicated to the Carraccis and to Guido Reni. The delicate features and the brush strokes are reflective of Lorenzo Pasinelli and Sebastiano Ricci as both artists were working in Bologna at that time.
af7b7b45-598f-5e3c-8472-5d1ad570467e.short_description: This celebrated altarpiece is one of the masterpieces of the young Burrini. Depicted at the feet of the Virgin, Saint Petronius, the patron of Bologna, and Saint Dionysius, the patron of France. The lively figures are reminiscent of Lorenzo Pasinelli, while the luminous colours and the quick brush strokes are an homage to the Venetian artist Sebastiano Ricci.
af7b7b45-598f-5e3c-8472-5d1ad570467e.provenance: Ratta Garganelli Chapel, San Giacomo Maggiore, Bologna
af7b7b45-598f-5e3c-8472-5d1ad570467e.obtention: This painting was originally made for the Ratta Garganelli chapel in the church of San Giacomo il Maggiore in Bologna. Later it was moved to the parish church of Monghidoro.

b2ca91ca-c46b-5e08-b073-5f3ded54c993.name: Monstrance of the Bemposta
b2ca91ca-c46b-5e08-b073-5f3ded54c993.alternate_name: Monstrance of the Chapel of the Palace of Bemposta or Palace of the Queen
b2ca91ca-c46b-5e08-b073-5f3ded54c993.description:
This magnificent monstrance in gilded silver and gold with a triangular base, sits on three volutes ornamented with floral motifs, ribbons and cartouches. On the three inferior angles of the base there are cherubs and three figures that symbolise Faith, Hope and Charity. On the top corners there are three full-bodied angels conveying Eucharistic motifs, while six cherubs and seraphs, overlap, ascending along the stem.  
On the three faces of the base oval bas-reliefs represent themes from the Eucharist: The Supper at Emmaus and the giant bunch of grapes, Fruit from the Promised Land and Christ at Calvary.  
The monstrance' sunburst is encircled by clouds. It has a radiant splendor with irregular rays, covered with precious stones. The monstrance's surface is entirely adorned with precious stones, some of them large and of excellent quality, creating a spectacular decorative and chromatic effect.  
The theatrical splendor of the Baroque is well illustrated through the use of jewels and quality chiselling, admirably assembled in a dazzling combination of metal and gemstones.  
It is likely the monstrance was commissioned by King Pedro III, husband of Queen Maria I. In Pedro III's Will of 1786 he foresees that his son, the future King João VI, should have the country house in Queluz, and urges him to care for the divine cult traditionally associated with the Bemposta Chapel, where he wished the precious monstrance to be kept.  
Attribution of this piece is controversial. Traditionally, researchers attributed it to J. F. Ludovice, the goldsmith and architect of the Convent of Mafra. Their theories were based on an existing drawing of the monstrance at the Museum, which also came from the Bemposta Palace.
b2ca91ca-c46b-5e08-b073-5f3ded54c993.short_description: A majestic monstrance in gilded silver with precious stones that creates a spectacular chromatic effect. The theatrical splendor of the Baroque is well illustrated through the use of jewels and quality chiselling, admirably assembled in a dazzling combination of metals and gemstones.
b2ca91ca-c46b-5e08-b073-5f3ded54c993.method_for_datation: Vassalo e Silva (2000) proposed that Adão Gottlieb Pollet both designed and made the monstrance. This is based on a specific analysis of the application of the gemstones. Although initially the  monstrance was dated to 1740–1750 the date is now thought to be later, 1775–1780.

b611d069-f267-5ab1-8a39-7ff245de0666.name: Pilgrimage Church of Our Lady of the Seven Sorrows
b611d069-f267-5ab1-8a39-7ff245de0666.alternate_name: Pilgrimage Church St. Mary in the Pear Tree
b611d069-f267-5ab1-8a39-7ff245de0666.description:
Westwards, the pietà-bearing pear tree was especially highlighted by its framing showcase architecture (now filled with an organ) . Located on the opposite side is the high altar. With their assigned bays, which are flanked by conches, both liturgical features originally formed two “sacred places” facing one another – a unique structure in Southern Germany. The domed structure in the centre serves as a meeting hall for the pilgrims. With its light-flooded lantern , which holds statues of the 12 apostles, it refers back to the Roman Pantheon and therefore functions as a universal symbol for the heavens and the Blessed Virgin Mary.  
The dedicated functions of the spatial sections are mirrored in the actual layout: It is composed of seven differently sized, interlinked circles. The curving of the lateral walls and the large arched openings combine the three spatial sections. Despite the room divisions, it creates a space continuum with the character of a centrally planned building. Attached is the sacristy, facing west behind the tree alcove, and an eastern tower surrounded by three conches behind the altar apsis. Besides the tall lantern of the central domed structure also the two conche-flanked bays were originally crowned with smaller lanterns, so that together with the three towers the building held a fantastic six-towered appearance. Altogether, the church represents one of the few ecclesiastical “fantasy concepts” that had truly been realised in the architectural history of Europe .
b611d069-f267-5ab1-8a39-7ff245de0666.short_description: A pear tree bearing a miraculous pietà was the eponymous event for the construction of the Early Baroque pilgrimage church St. Mary in the Pear Tree. A richly turreted  exterior design is connected with a complex triplicity of circular rooms. Coherent echoes of the Roman Pantheon play an explicit role. Moulded stucco applied to the inner walls and vaults provides the splendour that is to be expected.
b611d069-f267-5ab1-8a39-7ff245de0666.bibliography:
Schütz, B., *Maria Birnbaum: Deutschorden-Wallfahrtskirche*, Kleine Kunstführer 401, 13. neubearbeitete Auflage, Regensburg: Schnell & Steiner, 2004.  
Krins, H., *Barock in Süddeutschland*, Stuttgart: Theiss, 2001: 62–65.  
Schütz, B., *Die kirchliche Barockarchitektur in Bayern und Oberschwaben 1580–1780*, München: Hirmer, 2000: 96–98.  
Schütz, B., *Die Wallfahrtskirche Maria Birnbaum und ihre beiden Baumeister*, Kieler kunsthistorische Studien 4, Frankfurt am Main: Peter Lang, 1974.
b611d069-f267-5ab1-8a39-7ff245de0666.history:
The eponymous event for the construction of a pilgrimage sanctuary, outside the village of Sielenbach in the Ecknachtal region, was a pear tree bearing a miraculous image in the form of a so-called pietà. Because the latter presumably performed divine healings, a church was built surrounding the tree in 1661. An early change of plans initiated the addition of three towers and the semicircular sacristy in the west, followed by a conch that harboured the pear tree until 1866. Along with its miraculous image, the tree had died in 1668, only three years after the consecration, which led to several liturgical changes. The church was mostly restored to its original state in 1866. In this process, a remnant of the memorable tree trunk was incorporated into the furnishing of the high altar.  
The architecture that was planned by the Munich Electoral Master Builder, Konstantin Pader, seemingly traced back to suggestions of Philipp Jakob von Kaltenthal, a patron who travelled widely and was highly educated in architecture. As commander of the Teutonic Order, von Kaltenthal resided at the nearby castle Blumenthal. He had spent a lot of time in Rome where he had become acquainted with the model for the architectural idea that was later to be authenticated by himself: the domed rotunda in the Pantheon – the most symbolic Marian Church of the Eternal City at the time.
b611d069-f267-5ab1-8a39-7ff245de0666.patrons: Philipp Jakob von Kaltenthal, Commander of the Teutonic Order at Blumenthal (gov. 1658–69)
b611d069-f267-5ab1-8a39-7ff245de0666.architects: Architectural designs, stucco, and decoration: Konstantin Pader (1605–81);  Stuccowork: Matthias II Schmuzer (1636–86)

b72e7f3c-1702-565a-9c32-720167e16639.name: *Maria Immaculata*
b72e7f3c-1702-565a-9c32-720167e16639.description: This marble figurine, signed by Schletterer, corresponds with the popular type of Immaculate Virgin that evolved during the Catholic revival: the Virgin is at prayer atop a globe and a crescent moon, while she stands on the head of a serpent that symbolises evil. The slender female figure is modelled in a slight S-curve; her compact silhouette determined by the cloak. This feature, along with her charming face and the picturesque details such as the *putto* hiding beneath the drapery, derive from a Viennese variant of the arsenal of Late Baroque Venetian sculpture. The most notable representative of this trend in the imperial city of Vienna was Lorenzo Mattielli, while the leading master of the classical style was Georg Raphael Donner. Both artists influenced the oeuvre of the Tyrolese sculptor, Jakob Christoph Schletterer, who passed down his increasingly sophisticated classicistic style to subsequent generations during his long tutorship at the Academy of Fine Arts in Vienna. In the main, Schletterer made altar sculpture and reliefs for monastic churches in Lower Austria, but sepulchral monuments are also known to be by his hand. His documented works in Hungary – the Virgin Column in Sopron made after Andrea Altomonte's plans in 1745, and the garden statues at Darufalva (Drassburg) from 1758 – suggest that he probably delivered other works to Transdanubia. This signed, white marble *Immaculata* from Esterházy Castle, today at the Hungarian National Gallery in Budapest, is a more animated Rococo variant of the garden statue in Darufalva (Drassburg). In the collection of the Hungarian National Museum there is a similar Immaculata figurine, produced in Tata and transferred from the Cistercian abbey in Zirc, which also dates to the 1750s.
b72e7f3c-1702-565a-9c32-720167e16639.short_description: As a follower of Georg Raphael Donner and a professor at the Academy of Fine Arts in Vienna, Schletterer’s monumental works are found throughout Hungary (Győr, Sopron and Drassburg). This small, signed sculpture belonged to the Esterházy family in Tata.
b72e7f3c-1702-565a-9c32-720167e16639.provenance: Count Ferenc Esterházy, Esterházy Castle, Tata
b72e7f3c-1702-565a-9c32-720167e16639.obtention: From the collection of Count Ferenc Esterházy at Esterházy Castle, Tata; Kuny Domokos Museum, Tata

bbc7739e-3d42-5ce9-8c5c-bfb1ee694806.name: Oratorio della Santissima Trinità
bbc7739e-3d42-5ce9-8c5c-bfb1ee694806.description:
The Oratorio della Santissima Trinità has a square plan and a vaulted ceiling with lunettes. The interior is completely decorated. On the ceiling is depicted the Trinity. Figures of prophets are painted in the lunettes. The walls are decorated with biblical scenes framed by squares and separated by monochrome figures in a sort of frieze.  
The complex iconographic program is centred on the celebration of the Trinity and the Alliance between God and Man. All of the scenes depicted come from the Old Testament with the exception of the *Baptism of Christ*. Lionello Spada planned the general scheme of the cycle and painted it along with Francesco Brizio. Two of the scenes are attributed to Lucio Massari. It is very difficult to distinguish the different painters owing to their great technical and stylistic homogeneity. This testifies about their common will and technical preparation.  
The frescoes in this oratory are a good example of the renovation of painting created by the Carracci and developed by the Academy (Accademia dei desiderosi later the Accademia degli Incamminati), which was founded by the three Bolognese painters in 1582 in order to teach young artists. The perspective in the landscapes in the background of Francesco Brizio's paintings, where figures and landscape are equally important comes from the style of Ludovico Carracci. The painted illusionistic architecture of the ceiling shows Spada's apprenticeship as a Quadraturista (painter of illusionistic architectures).  
The imposing framing of the high altar and the wooden stalls of the choir, where the members of the brotherhood used to sit, carved and inlaid in oak, perfectly complete the decoration.
bbc7739e-3d42-5ce9-8c5c-bfb1ee694806.short_description: The Oratory of the Holy Trinity holds one of the most significant decorative cycles painted by the Bolognese school in the early 17th century. At the same time it is important evidence of the work of local brotherhoods assisting pilgrims. Its interior is completely decorated with beautiful frescoes painted by Lionello Spada, Lucio Massari and Francesco Brizio, pupils of the Carracci. The frescoes represent stories from the Old and New Testament. The wooden carved choir is among the finest works of Giacomo da Bergamo, called Venezian, a cabinet maker.
bbc7739e-3d42-5ce9-8c5c-bfb1ee694806.bibliography:
Campanini, G., Cavicchi, G. and Govoni, L., *La Compagnia della SS.ma Trinità. La chiesa e l'oratorio di Pieve di Cento*, Cento, 1979.  
Benati, D. “La pittura della prima metà del Seicento in Emilia e in Romagna”, *La Pittura in Italia. Il Seicento*, I, Milan, 1988, pp. 218–224.  
D'Amico, R. and Masetti Bitelli, L., *Restauri a Pieve di Cento. Il coro e gli affreschi della Chiesa della SS. Trinità. Un'esperienza di cantiere-scuola*, Casalecchio di Reno, 1993.
bbc7739e-3d42-5ce9-8c5c-bfb1ee694806.history:
The construction of the oratory linked to the the church and dedicated to the Holy Trinity and began in 1603. It was built by the Brotherhood of the Holy Trinity, whose task was to provide assistance for poor pilgrims and convalescent patients at the nearby hospital of St. Mary.  
Three well-known pupils of the Carraccis, Lionello Spada, Francesco Brizio and Lucio Massari began work on the painted decorations. The work began in 1605 and today these are considered one of the most significant fresco cycles of the early 17th century in Bologna. The beautiful carved wooden choir and the framing of the altar were commissioned in 1615 from Giacomo da Bergamo, known as 'Venezian'.  
The brotherhood of the Holy Trinity was suppressed in 1798, after the Napoleonic conquest, and all its properties passed to the Hospital of St. Mary.

keywords: Religious architecture; oratory; fresco; Carracci school; frieze; brotherhood

bd7a3cd3-6bbf-5036-bebe-7fdc38ffd56d.name: Monstrance
bd7a3cd3-6bbf-5036-bebe-7fdc38ffd56d.description:
The monstrance is by the Graz goldsmith, Hans Georg Pfisterer. The shaped oval base has enamel medallions showing scenes from the Passion of Christ and continues into a knob, shaped like a Baroque vase, from which rises the top part of the monstrance of the so-called sun type. Bands and foliate ornaments completely cover it intertwined with filigree and jewels. The opening of the ostensory has a six-sided moulded frame made up of wavy and angled sides and surrounded by airy filigree ornamentation of entwined scrolls and jewels that form flowers. Above the ostensory is a richly decorated canopy under which God the Father, holding the globe, hovers in clouds. Above the canopy is the dove of the Holy Ghost. At the foot of the frame, two adoring angels kneel on narrow decorated bases. The bottom edge of the monstrance has a lambrequin motif from which pearls hang.  
Bishop Juraj Branjug of Zagreb acquired the monstrance. He was one of Croatia’s most active bishops in 18th-century in the field of religious art building a new palace in Zagreb and renovating and building many churches. He had his own woodcarving workshop at Kaptol whose master craftsmen made altarpieces and pulpits adorned with the bishop’s arms for many churches. He bought and donated first-class liturgical objects to the cathedral.
bd7a3cd3-6bbf-5036-bebe-7fdc38ffd56d.short_description: A so-called sun monstrance covered with filigree work, a series of bands and foliate ornaments, jewels and enamel medallions showing the Passion of Christ. Made by the Graz goldsmith, Georg Pfisterer, it was acquired by Bishop Juraj Branjug for Zagreb Cathedral.

c03de3e5-cb58-583e-a3da-b1fc529f12c3.name: Pilgrimage Church of the Virgin Mary of Dolours, Sloup
c03de3e5-cb58-583e-a3da-b1fc529f12c3.description: The oval nave is closed with a presbytery and a simple column altar of local black and red marble. O. Schweigl’s construction frames the statue of the Pieta and Virgin Mary of Dolours Adored by Angels, which peaks in the figure of God the Father, the Dove of the Holy Spirit and a “lacework” baldachin.
c03de3e5-cb58-583e-a3da-b1fc529f12c3.short_description: Construction of the church was inspired by the miraculous recovery of a local miller’s daughter after praying to a statue of the Virgin Mary. The ceiling painting was executed by a later rector of the Vienna Academy C. F. Sambach. The Assumption scene, placed in an illusionary architectural frame, is supplemented with allegories of the Virtues in pendentives. Sambach also created the pictures for the side altars. This series of large paintings is among his best work. The festive atmosphere of the interior is enhanced by rich decoration and flower ornamentation by specialist artists.
c03de3e5-cb58-583e-a3da-b1fc529f12c3.method_for_datation: Preparatory sketches for the ceiling painting have been preserved in the Albertina Wien and Szépmüvészeti Múzeum in Budapest, the first of them is dated 1752.

Beiträge zum 30-jährigen Bestehen des Museums Langenargen,* Langenargen–Brno, 2007, pp. 263–293.
c03de3e5-cb58-583e-a3da-b1fc529f12c3.history: Sloup was a summer retreat for the Counts of Rogendorf. The church in which its founder is buried was built next to a former homestead (now the parsonage). Construction of the church was inspired by the miraculous recovery of a local miller’s daughter after praying to a statue of the Virgin Mary that was said to have been brought from the Minorite Monastery in Brno. The furnishing of both church and the residence were completed under the subsequent owners, the Salm family, who held this sought-after pilgrimage site until 1945.
c03de3e5-cb58-583e-a3da-b1fc529f12c3.patrons: Karolina of Rogendorf, *née* Pálfy-Erdödy (1741–1759), Antonín Josef Count Salm–Reifferscheidt

c173e928-a469-521a-8d30-74c53fdeb588.name: Catholic Parish and Pilgrimage Church of the Exaltation of the Cross and Our Lady of Sorrows
c173e928-a469-521a-8d30-74c53fdeb588.description:
The church is not only girded by cornices but also surrounded by a double series of large round-arched windows and four projections, each of them crowned by a tympanum. In the west – and very typically in the Baroque style – the main facade balloons out in a dish-shape manner from the exterior to the pulvinate middle part. Here it then rises, over a diadem-like curved cornice and a multi-scrolled ornamental gable, up into a squat looking turret with an onion-shaped roof.  
A centralised effect within the light-flooded galleries and four-bay aisle of the wall-pillar church is created through diagonally bent vaults, which allow the whole aisle to blend seamlessly with the richly decorated choir and its flat cupola vault. In addition to this effect, the two side altars also lead the viewer’s eye towards the high altar. The colorful and bright spatial impression is created through virtuoso stucco decoration in the Rococo style. This, together with the large ceiling frescos place the adoration of both the Cross and the Virgin Mary within the heavenly plan for salvation in accordance with the double patronage of the church. But, at first, the undersides of the galleries depict scenes from pilgrimage history directed towards pilgrims; the upper lateral barrel-vaults then show the suffering of the Virgin Mary. Finally, above these, one can find the oval ceiling fresco which echoes the paintings in the vault of the choir.
c173e928-a469-521a-8d30-74c53fdeb588.short_description: From 1749, under the auspices of the Premonstratensian monastery Rot an der Rot, the spacious pilgrimage church in Maria Steinbach was rebuilt and enlarged in order to do justice to the enormous inflow of pilgrims. The church is deemed to be one of the jewels of Bavarian Rococo. Its art historical fame originates from its overwhelmingly rich interior with its eloquent frescos rich in images, virtuosic use of stucco and whimsically designed altars.
c173e928-a469-521a-8d30-74c53fdeb588.method_for_datation: Archival evidence and also an inscription on the south portal. Above the main portal are placed the coats-of-arms of the abbots Hermann Vogler (gov. 1711–1739), and Mauritius Moritz (gov. 1760–1782) referring to the church’s elevation to a pilgrimage sanctuary, and respectively, completion of the church building.
c173e928-a469-521a-8d30-74c53fdeb588.bibliography:
Schütz, B., *Die kirchliche Barockarchitektur in Bayern und Oberschwaben 1580–1780*, Munich 2000, pp. 51, 155.  
Buck, I. A., *Katholische Pfarr- und Wallfahrtskirche Maria Steinbach*, Lindenberg 1998.  
Beck, O., *Katholische Pfarr- und Wallfahrtskirche Maria Steinbach* (Kleine Kunstführer 205, 7th revised edition), Regensburg 1992.
c173e928-a469-521a-8d30-74c53fdeb588.history: The pilgrimage to Maria Steinbach is incorporated in the Premonstratensian abbey Rot an der Rot which was founded in 1126. From 1723 onwards the former parish church was considered a pilgrimage centre due to Abbot Hermann Vogler's donation of a particle of the cross. For the purposes of adoration, a 100-year-old crucifix was restored and erected upon the high altar along with two assistant sculptural figures, a *Mater Dolorosa* and the *Apostle St John*. The steadily growing flow of pilgrims, supposedly due to the miraculous healing powers attributed to the sculpture of the Virgin Mary, was the reason that, in 1734, Maria Steinbach was elevated to a special place of pilgrimage dedicated to the Virgin Mary. To meet the demands of such a steadily growing number of pilgrims it was decided to rebuild the church according to the so-called “Vorarlberger Münster” scheme (named after the regional school of Austrian master builders). The architecturally trained local Premonstratensian monk, Father Benedict Stadelhofer was chosen as architect in 1746. After the transferral of the miraculous image of the Virgin in 1754, the church was then consecrated in 1755 although consecration of the high altar and thus the ultimate finish of the building process took place later, in 1770.
c173e928-a469-521a-8d30-74c53fdeb588.patrons: Abbots of the Premonstratensian Abbey Rot an der Rot, Ignatius Vetter (gov. 1739–1755), Benedict Stadelhofer (gov. 1755–1760), Mauritius Moritz (gov. 1760–1782)
c173e928-a469-521a-8d30-74c53fdeb588.architects: Design of architecture: Pater Benedikt Stadelhofer (1694–1760); master builder: Anton Lacher (1705–1777); stucco: Johann Georg Üblher (1703–1763), of the altar and ornamental niche: Franz Xaver Feichtmayr the Younger (1735–1803), Franz Xaver Schmuzer (1713–1775); frescos: Franz Georg Hermann the Younger (1692–1768)
keywords: Pilgrimage church; ceiling fresco; stucco

c23367a7-fd96-5a53-a4f8-2a90b49cbda0.name: Bom Jesus de Braga Sanctuary
c23367a7-fd96-5a53-a4f8-2a90b49cbda0.description:
A grandiose staircase leads up to the church. Flanked by dense vegetation, it is subdivided into three stairways with terraces dedicated to the five senses and five virtues. The Moses Terrace is at the top with access to the church.  
The entrance to the staircase combines a monumental porch and a rounded gateway. At the top of the gate is the coat of arms of one of the main organisers of the last stage of the program: the Archbishop of Braga, Rodrigo de Moura Teles.  
There are two fountains either side of the stairway. Each is crowned with an inscription, one of which explains that we are in the presence of “JERUSALEM SANCTA RESTAURADA E REEDIFICADA NO ANNO DE 1723” (Sanctified Jerusalem Renovated and Rebuilt in the Year of 1723).  
On both sides at the upper level before the main stairway, there are two great quadrangular chapels with eye-windows.  
A series of stairs, each composed of 39 flights of steps, leads to the intermediate and main terraces. The stairs zigzag up the hill interrupted by terraces, each of which has a central, hexagonal or octagonal shaped chapel, as well as a fountain. Each chapel is identified by an inscription retelling an episode from the Passion of Christ along with associated sculptures; while bas-relief Roman Gods with their attributes, furnish the backs of the fountains, in some cases there is an inscription.  
The Stairway of the Five Senses was built from 1725 onwards. Its allegorical theme conveys individual redemption, promoting a notion that evil becomes good by controlling the instincts (the senses) and by appreciation of the spirit instead of the physical and carnal. The six fountains – sculpted in granite with *rocaille* details – are located on the central axis of the ensemble, installed against an ornamental Baroque background. Allegorical figures, each representing one of the five senses, crown the fountains.  
The Stairway of the Virtues follows immediately after that of the five senses. It was built in the second half of the 18th century under Archbishop Gaspar de Bragança. The overall sculptural theme is identical to the others (a central figure flanked by two others) although the half-fountains are embedded in great central niches at the back of the stairs. Then, finally, one reaches the church. Construction began in 1784 and ended in 1811, it has a Neo-Classical façade and two bell towers.
c23367a7-fd96-5a53-a4f8-2a90b49cbda0.short_description: Venerated by the Portuguese, this pilgrimage sanctuary of the type known as *Sacro Monte* (Way of the Cross), includes a large complex Baroque stairway – along which are chapels, statues and allegorical fountains – leading to the upper square where the Neo-Classical style Bom Jesus Church is located.
c23367a7-fd96-5a53-a4f8-2a90b49cbda0.dates: Founded in the 15th century; Baroque works carried out 1723–1811

c23367a7-fd96-5a53-a4f8-2a90b49cbda0.history:
The Bom Jesus de Braga Sanctuary dates to 1494 and was the brainchild of the influential Archbishop of Braga, Jorge da Costa, in reaction to the country's impulse for popular devotion.  
It was in the 17th century, however, that the Bom Jesus Church was first established as a pilgrimage sanctuary of the *Sacro Monte* (Way of the Cross) type. In 1629 a hermit – Pedro do Rosário – was nominated, the church was reconstructed, and the Passos da Cruz chapels were set up. These features were the basis for the devotional nature of the site, founded on “Baroque” principles at a time when pilgrimages, which had been held since the end of the 15th century, were undergoing change.  
The ongoing repairs, especially those of the 18th century, turn this ensemble into one of the world's best known Baroque buildings.  
In 1723 Rodrigo de Moura Teles, Archbishop of Braga, decided to renovate the whole sanctuary. He scheduled in the Bom Jesus programme as part of his overall political agenda and saw it as a long-term priority. He commissioned a monumental Baroque stairway leading up to a portico entrance, which led into the new elliptically shaped church. The elaborate iconographic program includes a series of sculptures depicting both Christian and ancient pagan allegories.
c23367a7-fd96-5a53-a4f8-2a90b49cbda0.patrons: D. Jorge da Costa, Archbishop of Braga (1493–1498); D. Rodrigo de Moura Teles (1644–1728); Archbishop of Braga (1704–1728); D. Gaspar de Bragança (1716-1789); Archbishop of Braga (1758–1789).
c23367a7-fd96-5a53-a4f8-2a90b49cbda0.architects: Architects (attributed): Manuel Pinto de Vila Lobos (?–1734), André Soares (1720–1769), Carlos Amarante (1748–1815); master masons: António Ferreira Lopes ; woodcarvers: Elias Gomes dos Santos, João Bernardo da Silva, João Álvares Bezerra, João Martins Coelho; sculptors: António de Campos Peixoto, António José Pereira, António Monteiro, António Pinto, Domingos António, Domingos Ferreira, Evangelista Vieira, Félix António and others; painters: Pedro Alexandrino de Carvalho, and others whose dates are unknown.
keywords: *Sacro Monte*, pilgrimage sanctuary, Braga archbishops, *via crucis*, Bom Jesus, Braga

c2f6e9fe-ab29-564b-aeb1-f14417f8e49c.name: *Pietà*
c2f6e9fe-ab29-564b-aeb1-f14417f8e49c.description:
With a preference for sculpture of enormous dimensions that entirely occupy the grand gilded altarpieces of the period, Frei Cipriano da Cruz is considered to be the most extraordinary representative of the National Baroque style.  
His sculpture was generally based on models that circulated throughout Europe and can be considered within the context of other depictions of the Crucifixion and Passion of Christ. A monk-sculptor, the *Pietà* is one of Frei Cipriano's greatest achievements. It exemplifies a theme widespread in Portuguese art in the 16th and 17th centuries, meeting most of the essential Tridentine ideals.  
The *Pietà* belongs to an ensemble of pieces made by Frei Cipriano for the S. Bento Church, which belonged to the college of the Benedictine order in Coimbra and was demolished in 1932.  
This ensemble features anatomical details that are typical of Frei Cipriano, in particular the hands and faces. In the *Pietà* Christ's hands are rough with square-shaped finger nails. His face is framed by abundant curly hair; the S-shaped curls are also present in the beard. The Virgin displays a heavy look; she has high symmetrical eyebrows, a long triangular-shaped nose, and thin defined lips.  
The heavy and pyramidal structure of the *Pietà* is accentuated by the drapery: the red, blue and gold cloak that completely wraps the figure. The drapery is notable in that its decorative motifs correspond with textiles of the period – elaborate brocades and oriental silks. The drapery and embroidery, generally designated as “upholstery”, were pre-made in resin-wax and were applied to the figure later after painting and finishing.  
The motif of the artichoke particularly stands out. It imitates the three-bordered brocade of Spanish and Italian origin and is strategically placed on the Virgin's knee to have the greatest visual impact.  
According to recent research (Alcoforado and Le Gac, 2003) Manuel da Costa Pereira, who was responsible for painting and gilding the *Pietà*, often worked with other painters. Further research about them will bring us closer to understanding the originality of Frei Cipriano da Cruz's sculpture.
c2f6e9fe-ab29-564b-aeb1-f14417f8e49c.short_description: With a preference for sculpture of enormous dimensions that entirely occupy the grand gilded altarpieces of the period, Frei Cipriano da Cruz is considered to be the most extraordinary representative of the National Baroque style. The Pietà represents one of his greatest achievements.

c37ef84c-4918-5c4a-89b2-3c585804a510.name: *Bust of a Saint*
c37ef84c-4918-5c4a-89b2-3c585804a510.description:
The bust, on an original volute pedestal, arises out of a relatively narrow base widening into a compact chest. The bearded head is that of an old man, with a cloak thrown loosely over the right shoulder. The figure might be St. Hieronymus, one of the church fathers. The pedestal shows that the object was a reliquary.  
*Bust of a Saint* demonstrates the artist's broad creativity seen not only his technical craft but also in his ability to capture mental states. The ecstatic expression of desire and submission to God is not rough-hewn, but has an elegant, court-like nature manifest in the figure's S-shaped movement and the soft shaping of the volume.  
Lengelacher may have familiarised himself with bust-making in his native Bavaria, or during a stay in Vienna through Giovanni Giuliani, who provided the gallery pews in the Heiligenkreutz Monastery, Lower Austria, with a whole series of busts. Lengelacher probably met Giuliani while working on the decorations of the Belveder in Vienna.  
In 1719 Lengelacher settled in Mikulov, where as sculptor to Walter František of Dietrichstein, he created sculpted interior decorations for several south Moravian churches. Lengelacher's *Bust of a Saint* is part of a series of original decorations for altar tables in the Church of St. Michael, Dolní Věstonice, which Lengelacher embellished with stuccoes and carvings. The artist worked there from the 1720s in relation to one of his first major commissions, the Benedictine church in Rajhrad (1727–1734).
c37ef84c-4918-5c4a-89b2-3c585804a510.short_description: *Bust of a Saint* demonstrates both the artist's skill as a sculptor and his ability to capture mental states. The ecstatic expression of desire and submission to God is not rough-hewn but has an elegant, court-like nature. The reliquary bust is part of the original altar decorations in Dolní Věstonice.

c37ef84c-4918-5c4a-89b2-3c585804a510.method_for_datation: The authorship and dating of the sculpture have been determined by its provenance and confirmed by an analysis of the style.
c37ef84c-4918-5c4a-89b2-3c585804a510.obtention: The bust and its counterpart were purchased in 1913 from a private vendor. It comes from the Church of St. Michael in Dolní Věstonice in South Moravia.

cbb6bbe3-72b1-5d00-b8a3-fc74f38248d4.name: Sacramento Monstrance
cbb6bbe3-72b1-5d00-b8a3-fc74f38248d4.description:
An exceptional example of Baroque workmanship during the period of King João V, the Sacramento Monstrance – also called the *Anjo Custódia* “Angel Monstrance” – assumes the form of an Atlantis angel, a figure that is sometimes incorporated into the lower part of gilded wooden altarpieces. In this particular case the Atlantis angel appears free; instead of the usual representation as a pillar sustaining a globe the angel holds a radiant sun. Theatrical tension is undoubtedly achieved with the decoration of the piece itself, but the monstrance would have been surrounded by the gilded wood of the sacred space of the high altar and the aim would have been to increase the emotional and devotional fervour of the congregation and lead them to contemplate the divine light of truth and its beauty.  
Symbol of the Church Triumphant, the monstrance is a splendid composition of contrasting effects: dynamic lines and imposing shape – the result of which sees the elegant sculptural angel in polychrome and gilded wood – and the resplendence of silver, colour and glinting of both the enamel and glass.  
The kneeling angel holds a spherical, smooth and polished monstrance enveloped in a corona of silver rays. Surrounding the *luna* – the space where the host is kept and exhibited – are Eucharistic symbols enhanced by brightly coloured enamel work, and mounted over a circular base with eight ornamental silver-gilt cherubs. Vegetal motifs and coloured glass form flowers to complete the decoration. The monstrance presents a municipal contrast between the silver from Lisbon (L), in use since 1690, and the incomplete hallmark of an unidentified goldsmith from Lisbon, whose initials were LRP, and who was active between the end of the 17th century and the first half of the 18th century.
cbb6bbe3-72b1-5d00-b8a3-fc74f38248d4.short_description: Holding the solar sphere made out of silver – glowing with the true Word of God – the Atlantes angel is supposed to increase the emotional and devotional fervour of the congregation and lead them to contemplate the divine light of truth and its beauty. This piece was probably the highlight of the gilded wood high altar at Sacramento Convent in Lisbon.
cbb6bbe3-72b1-5d00-b8a3-fc74f38248d4.owner: Museu Nacional Machado de Castro, Coimbra
cbb6bbe3-72b1-5d00-b8a3-fc74f38248d4.method_for_datation: This goldsmith’s hallmark first appeared in the early part of the decade of 1690 and continued to appear throughout the first decades of the 18th century. The technical and stylistic affinities of both the figure of the Atlantis angel and the polychrome allow the monstrance to be placed within the Baroque style during the reign of João V (1707–1750).
cbb6bbe3-72b1-5d00-b8a3-fc74f38248d4.obtention: The monstrance came originally from the Santíssimo Sacramento Convent in Alcântara, Lisbon. Founded in 1612, the convent belonged to the female branch of the Dominican order and was closed after the death of the last nun in 1897. The monstrance was transferred to Coimbra in 1914 where it became part of the gold and silverware collection of the National Museum of Machado de Castro.

cfe04c10-c802-5c71-9567-60d035ba26a9.name: Head of St. Philip Neri
cfe04c10-c802-5c71-9567-60d035ba26a9.description:
This head modelled in wax is considered a replica of a bronze in the collection of the Rhode Island School of Design in Providence, made by Alessandro Algardi around 1640. Another bronze version is in the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica in Rome. These bronzes were made a few years before the artist was charged with the statue in marble of St. Philip Neri for the sacristy of Santa Maria in Vallicella, in Rome (1635–38). For this commission Algardi carefully studied the death mask of the saint, dead in 1595 and sanctified in 1622. The saint's face is strained by old age and suffering but shows deep humanity, humility and the extraordinary strength of a man near to God. Its classicising features make it similar to an antique portrait.  
Algardi, a pupil of Ludovico Carracci's, began a career as a sculptor and in 1625 moved to Rome where he spent nearly all his artistic life.
cfe04c10-c802-5c71-9567-60d035ba26a9.short_description: This wax head is thought to be a replica of two bronze ones portraying the same saint, made by Alessandro Algardi around 1640. The sculptor previously carved a marble statue of St. Philip with an angel for the sacristy of Santa Maria in Vallicella in Rome (1635-38). In these head portraits which are strictly devotional, he deepens his analysis of the facial features, emphasising the strong humanity of the saint and his strong moral and spiritual strength.
cfe04c10-c802-5c71-9567-60d035ba26a9.holder: Museo di Arte Industriale e Galleria Davia Bargellini
cfe04c10-c802-5c71-9567-60d035ba26a9.method_for_datation: The bronze head in Providence is nearly identical to the wax one, which bears a date. Critics think that heads like this were commissioned to sculptors after the success of the marble statue with St. Philip Neri and the angel for S. Maria in Vallicella, finished in 1638.
cfe04c10-c802-5c71-9567-60d035ba26a9.obtention: The work was probably purchased at the beginning of the twentieth-century; no documentation survives.

d097475a-8ad7-5263-8b4d-b1c5381c6516.name: Former residence of the painter family Zeiller
d097475a-8ad7-5263-8b4d-b1c5381c6516.description: The paintings adorning the Zeiller House, in which Johann Jakob Zeiller had his home and workshop, are closer stylistically to the work of his cousin Franz Anton which is why they are usually attributed to the latter. It is an especially rich example of the “Lüftlmalerei” common in Außenfern. As Außenfern belonged to the diocese of Augsburg, the stylistic sources as well as pictorial models are primarily to be sought there. The special features of the paintings on the Zeiller House are their virtuoso composition featuring religious and profane motifs and exoticisms.
d097475a-8ad7-5263-8b4d-b1c5381c6516.short_description: The most famous of the numerous residential houses with façade paintings in Lechtal, Tyrol, was the home of the famous family of painters Zeiller. The façades of the elongated house are decorated on three sides with “Lüftlmalerei” (outside paintings), with the especially richly decorated gable end with bay window forming the main visible face. A very pretty example of the artistic self-presentation of this period.
d097475a-8ad7-5263-8b4d-b1c5381c6516.dates: The house with a gable-end façade was built in the 16th century and subsequently altered numerous times. The Late Rococo façade paintings originate from the period around 1770/75.
d097475a-8ad7-5263-8b4d-b1c5381c6516.bibliography: Baur-Heinhold, *Margarete, Süddeutsche Fassadenmalerei vom Mittelalter bis zur Gegenwart*, Munich 1952, pp. 114–18.
d097475a-8ad7-5263-8b4d-b1c5381c6516.history: The Zeiller House, also called “Schönes Haus”, was erected in the 16th century. It is situated in the north of Reutte on the so-called “Untermarkt” (Lower Market). It survived the major fires of 1703/04. Paul Zeiller (1658–1738), the father of Johann Jakob and founder of the Außerfern school of painting had his workshop here. On the south side of the building fragments of paintings are preserved which date from around 1600. The façade paintings on the other sides originate from around 1770/75 and are either the work of Johann Jakob or his nephew Franz Anton Zeiller.
d097475a-8ad7-5263-8b4d-b1c5381c6516.architects: Façade paintings, attributed to: Franz Anton Zeiller (1716–1794) or Johann Jakob Zeiller (1708–1783)
keywords: Façade paintings; Lüftlmalerei; fresco paintings; secular building; residential house; family of artists

df9202cd-5ffe-50f5-8101-fe2861cfd87e.name: St. Thomas of Villanova Church
df9202cd-5ffe-50f5-8101-fe2861cfd87e.description: The intentional simplicity of the façade, punctuated by pilaster strips and the papal coat of arms and characterised by a high ribbed cupola, contrasts with the elegance of the interior – a Greek cross – in which Raggi’s rich and detailed decorative stuccowork in white and gold cover the high altar. Pairs of angels on the window-displays hold up eight medallions with *miraculous episodes* of Saint Thomas of Villanova, and on the pendentives, the *Four Evangelists*. These medallions, which also symbolise monetary value as well as being the instrument used by Saint Thomas in his charitable work, are merely the transposition into an architectural and decorative structure of the ephemeral device specially prepared for the canonisation in Saint Peter Basilica in 1658. This canonisation is attributable both to purely religious reasons, in response to the Lutheran Reformation, and historical and political reasons on account of the important role played by Spain in the delicate international balance of that period. The church also contains, in among partially gilded classical architecture, paintings by the greatest painters in Rome at the time, making a fascinating and harmonious whole, attributable to a unitary project by an artist-director such as Bernini, in which the different arts blend naturally: on the high altar, between a stucco medallion supported by angels and crowned by the Almighty, the *Crucifixion* (1661) by Pietro da Cortona in which the dramatic tension of the subject is hardly lessened by the playful motif of the putto leaning out the frame to watch. On the right-hand altar is the painting by Giacinto Gimignani, *Glory of St. Thomas* dating from 1661–2, which is considered the brief assumption and the representative complement of what is shown in the cupola as the charitable activity in the life of the Saint, symbolically expressed by the coin jar at the centre, constituting the antecedent that has allowed the performance of miracles included summarily in the painting, and for which the Church canonised Thomas of Villanova. On the left-hand altar, finally, the *Assumption of the Virgin* by Guglielmo Cortese, also from 1661, happily combines classical sobriety and Baroque sensibility
df9202cd-5ffe-50f5-8101-fe2861cfd87e.short_description: The intentional simplicity of the façade, punctuated by pilaster strips and the papal coat of arms, and characterised by a high ribbed cupola, contrasts with the elegance of the interior – a Greek cross – in which rich and detailed stucco decoration in white and gold covers the high altar, the cupola and the pendentives. Among the partially gilded classical architecture of the interior, in a harmonious and attractive whole arising from the unitary scheme of an artist-director such as Bernini, are found paintings by Rome’s greatest painters at the time.

df9202cd-5ffe-50f5-8101-fe2861cfd87e.history: St. Thomas of Villanova Church was previously the parish church of San Nicola. Rebuilt by Bernini during the restoration of the apostolic palace from the beginning of 1658, soon after the canonisation of the Spaniard Tommaso da Villanova (1486–1555) on 1 November 1658, Pope Alexander VII decided to dedicate the church to the new saint as a symbol of active charity, where unlike the Lutheran approach, salvation was achieved not through faith only, but also through works. Thereafter the original dedication to Saint Nicola was reserved for the lower church near the lake.

e56f778f-130c-58d7-891f-71e9a25278ff.name: Capuchin Monastery and the Church of the Invention of the Holy Cross, Brno
e56f778f-130c-58d7-891f-71e9a25278ff.description: The church, situated below the Episcopal Courtyard, is a single-nave building with a straight chancel. By the east wall are the original Chapels of St. Francis of Assisi and St. Fidelius, which was added later by M. Grimm. A crypt containing mummified bodies, most of them monks, as well as that of Baron Trenck, lies under the church and is something of a tourist attraction.
e56f778f-130c-58d7-891f-71e9a25278ff.short_description: The Capuchins came to Brno in 1604 by invitation of Cardinal Dietrichstein, who also introduced the order to Mikulov as part of his Counter-Reformation enterprises. The original seat of the order was destroyed in the Swedish siege of Brno in 1645. Count Liechtenstein-Castelkorn, the Provincial Governor of Moravia, financed the construction of a new Capuchin Monastery. The high altar altarpiece, by the renowned German artist J. Sandrart, is considered the first Baroque painting in Moravia. There is a crypt containing mummified bodies, most of them monks, as well as that of Baron Trenck.
e56f778f-130c-58d7-891f-71e9a25278ff.method_for_datation: The paintings by J. Sandrart and J. L. Kracker are signed and dated.

e56f778f-130c-58d7-891f-71e9a25278ff.history: The Capuchins came to Brno in 1604 by invitation of Cardinal Dietrichstein, who also introduced the order to Mikulov as part of his Counter-Reformation enterprises. The original seat of the order, by the Menínská brána Gate, was destroyed in the Swedish siege of Brno in 1645. Count Liechtenstein-Castelkorn, Provincial Governor of Moravia, financed the construction of a new Capuchin Monastery in the coal market. The 18th-century reconstruction of the monastery was designed by father and son Grimm, prominent Moravian builders. Their house adjoined the monastery and they are buried in the crypt.

e74a5378-d264-576d-8085-d09134e9e428.name: Mikulov Town
e74a5378-d264-576d-8085-d09134e9e428.description: The dominant landmarks of the town are Sv. Kopeček (Holy Hill), the Loreto) Chapel, the Holy Trinity Column, the Upper Synagogue, the monasteries, the Jewish quarter and a mannerist chateau, originally part of a medieval castle. An extravagant entrance to the chateau was constructed together with a theatre and a “Hall of Ancestors”, decorated with murals featuring portraits of significant family members. Cardinal Dietrichstein also created one of the largest libraries in Europe with a collection of books that was further expanded by items confiscated from Protestant libraries and which was looted in turn by the Swedish army in 1645. Today’s collection, dating from the 18th century, consists of the Dietrichstein family’s libraries acquired through purchase or inheritance. Situated opposite the chateau, in the lower section of the square facing Svatý Kopeček, is a chapel, originally modelled on an Italian Loreto to symbolise the birthplace of Christ, in which the family’s dead are interred. J. B. Fischer von Erlach designed its reconstruction in 1700 but who was responsible for its current form is not clear. The original Renaissance frontage with a tower was replaced by a monumental facade between 1704 and 1708. The sculptures are by the Brno artist, A. Riga, and the reliefs by M. Roth.
e74a5378-d264-576d-8085-d09134e9e428.short_description: Inhabited since pre-history, Mikulov is a small town in south Moravia. Cardinal Dietrichstein, ruler of Moravia after the Battle of White Mountain in 1620 and a leading figure in the Czech Counter-Reformation, made his seat the hub of Moravia. Parts of a medieval castle were incorporated into a mannerist chateau where the cardinal created one of the largest libraries in Europe. He had a pilgrimage chapel built, modelled on an Italian Loreto and one of the first of its kind in Czech lands. Part of the town was an important cultural centre for the Jewish community.
e74a5378-d264-576d-8085-d09134e9e428.method_for_datation: Dating is based on historical events: the buildings were reconstructed after the fires and looting of the Thirty Years’ War. Contracts and receipts for individual reconstructions are extant, in particular those of G. G. Tencalla and I. Lengelacher, who also signed the Holy Trinity Column. A number of buildings did not survive the vicissitudes of history but are, however, mentioned in written sources (garden design by Jean Trehet (1700–1708); paintings by Anton Josef Prenner).

e74a5378-d264-576d-8085-d09134e9e428.history: The Dietrichsteins acquired the demesne in 1575 when Cardinal Dietrichstein became ruler of Moravia after the Battle of White Mountain in 1620. He was a leading figure in the Czech Counter-Reformation and made Mikulov his seat and the hub of Moravia. Summoning the Capuchin and Piarist orders (1611; 1636), he created a centre for the Catholic Church with both sacred and secular buildings. Mikulov was damaged by fire in 1663, 1719, 1784 and 1945 and the Cardinal’s residence has consequently undergone several reconstructions which have, however, held true to the original functional and spatial intentions.

ef74c9ed-a4dc-57df-a3a1-c5538d838390.name: *Tomb statue of Prince Pál Esterházy and his first wife (Orsolya Esterházy?)*
ef74c9ed-a4dc-57df-a3a1-c5538d838390.description:
The four wooden statues representing the Esterházy brothers (Pál and Ferenc) and their wives were certainly commissioned by the Pál Esterházy family. The founder of the dynasty, Palatin Pál, built a family mausoleum in the Franciscan Church in Kismarton (Eisenstadt), within the residential area that formed part of his large estates. Although the crypt was completely rebuilt in 1856–57 its previous appearance can be reconstructed on the basis of a detailed description of the interior from 1835–36 and a plan of the building. As these documents prove, the Kismarton (Eisenstadt) Mausoleum consisted of a lower and an upper chapel. The rounded niches on the upper level were for the gilded-wood, kneeling figures of Pál and Ferenc Esterházy, Orsolya Esterházy and Kata Thököly. The statues in the Hungarian National Gallery, one of which also bears some marks of gilding, seem to be identical to these niche figures. The statues are composed on a frontal view. Their backs are grooved, and their feet are not perfectly carved, a sign that the statues were designed for wall-niches. Pál Esterházy is represented in somewhat historic clothes (coat-of-arms and a short skirt), with a wig, and the Order of the Golden Fleece, which he obtained in 1681. His wife wears Hungarian apparel, a shoulder corset decorated with flowers, a blouse with pleated shoulders, a girdle decorated with precious stones and a necklace.  
In the lower chapel is the still extant sarcophagus of Palatin Pál, which could be viewed from the upper level through the lattice window. There was an altar dedicated to the Virgin Mary in each chapel. Members of the Esterházy family kneeling in the niches of the upper chapel in gestures of eternal worship were, thus, turned to the Virgin Mary mourning her son, suggesting therefore that they committed themselves to her patronage not only in life but even in death.  
The design of Pál Esterházy's sepulchral chapel represents an organic part of his art patronage, in which the cult of the Virgin Mary was determinative.
ef74c9ed-a4dc-57df-a3a1-c5538d838390.short_description: The sculptures represent the founder of the Esterházy dynasty, Pál Esterházy, and his first wife, Orsolya Esterházy (together with the figures of his brother and sister-in-law) kneeling in prayer. The works originate from the Kismarton (Eisenstadt) family vault and are representative examples of 17th-century portrait sculpture of the region.

f7e4c02e-6b61-5d4c-85bf-101b2a06a6b8.name: Wilten Basilica (Parish Church of the Immaculate Conception)
f7e4c02e-6b61-5d4c-85bf-101b2a06a6b8.alternate_name: Our Lady Under the Four Columns
f7e4c02e-6b61-5d4c-85bf-101b2a06a6b8.description: The architectural character of Wilten parish church is a typical work of Penz, with a clear and simple ground plan, balanced proportions and a harmonious spatial arrangement, all carefully calculated to generate a pleasing prospect. The further development of the scheme of the Innsbruck city parish church resulted in a unification of the spatial image, which in Innsbruck was more clearly characterised by the sequence of bays with cupola-like vaults. While Penz supplied ideas and acted as construction supervisor, the plans originate from the sculptor Joseph Stapf from the Füssen school. The building work was carried out by Matthias and Johann Michael Umhauser.
f7e4c02e-6b61-5d4c-85bf-101b2a06a6b8.short_description: Wilten Basilica is considered the most important Rococo ecclesiastical building in North Tyrol, and alongside Gossensaß, the most accomplished of Franz de Paula Penz’s works. The plain building, a two-bay pilaster church with a barely retracted choir surprises with a magnificent prospect composed of finely coordinated architecture, ornamentation and sculptures of great stylistic unity.
f7e4c02e-6b61-5d4c-85bf-101b2a06a6b8.type: Ecclesiastical architecture (parish church, papal basilica and pilgrimage church)
f7e4c02e-6b61-5d4c-85bf-101b2a06a6b8.method_for_datation: Archives, choir arch cartouche with chronogram, “1755”

f7e4c02e-6b61-5d4c-85bf-101b2a06a6b8.history: According to the founding legend even Roman legionnaires in Wilten worshipped an image of the Virgin Mary “Under the Four Columns”, and according to records it served as a site of pilgrimage as early as the 13th century. Excavations revealed an original building dating from the early Christian period, a consecration was held in 1311, and in the late 15th century a Gothic vault was inserted. Up until 1643 the building also served as the parish church of Innsbruck. In 1728 the church was refurbished in the Baroque style. Following building damage in 1750 a new building was erected between 1751 and 1756. Interior work was carried out up until the late 18th century.

f811818c-63f6-5385-94c0-2eb1a870aecb.name: Chapel of the Rosary, basilica di San Domenico, Bologna
f811818c-63f6-5385-94c0-2eb1a870aecb.description: The complex painted decoration of Mitelli and Colonna involves four pilasters, two archivolts, the walls and the vaults of the whole chapel. The painters were helped by the sculptor Domenico Ottani, who made the stucco decorations, the capitals and the elegant friezes, and the gilders Alessandro Miselli and Carlo Veronese. The abundant use of gold leaf for the decorations gives the chapel its typical baroque sumptuousness and contributes to the diffusion of light. Mitelli and Colonna started working in February 1655, completing the painting in May 1657. The subject chosen was the glorification of the Blessed Virgin of the Rosary. The dome is decorated with a beautiful sky wherein the Madonna is carried up by the angels and crowned. In the roundels at the base of the dome are represented the merits of the Rosary handed by the Virgin to St. Dominic in order to defeat the plague of 1630. Putti, angels and Virtues celebrate the glory of the Virgin among flowers, in one of the most impressive scenes of Emilian baroque. The altar is framed by illusionistic architecture on the apse and crowned by two choirs of angels holding crowns, one of flowers and one of stars thus following the motto “*Dat flores tellus, coelum dat sidera sertis*”. Three great ovals frame episodes from the life of the Virgin (the *Birth of Mary*, *Mary presented to the temple* and the *Marriage of the Virgin*). This extraordinary fresco decoration ideally faces the *Glorification of St. Dominic* painted by Guido Reni in the chapel dedicated to the saint, just across the nave.
f811818c-63f6-5385-94c0-2eb1a870aecb.short_description:
The Chapel of the Rosary was created in 1589 when the Brotherhood of the Rosary refurbished the medieval chapel held by the Guidotti family.  
Particularly striking is the altar framing the statue of the Madonna of the Rosary, surrounded by 15 small pictures with the mysteries of the Rosary, work of many celebrated Bolognese painters.  
In the second half of the seventeenth-century the interior of the chapel was rebuilt with a new dome and a new apse, while the exterior held the polygonal late Gothic features. Between 1655 and 1657 the whole chapel was decorated by the painters Angelo Michele Colonna and Agostino Mitelli, who made the present rich scenographic decoration, glorifying the Blessed Virgin of the Rosary.

f811818c-63f6-5385-94c0-2eb1a870aecb.history: In 1460 Giovanni Guidotti asked the mason Giovanni del Lago di Como to build a chapel in the church of San Domenico imitating that dedicated to St. Thomas, in Gothic style. The chapel was named the Guidotti chapel. In 1575, with the Guidotti's permission, the confraternity of the Rosary started to use the chapel for its meetings and in 1589 paid for its total refurbishment. Among the most significant works of art of this period stand the sumptuous altar dedicated to the Virgin and the decoration of the vault. In 1601 the most celebrated workshops in Bologna commissioned 15 paintings that now surround the statue of the Virgin and represent the Mysteries of the Rosary. They are representative of Bolognese contemporary painting style. After the plague of 1630 the Madonna of the Rosary became the focus of a rejuvenated religious zeal. Many gifts were presented to the chapel from the people who had survived the epidemic. In 1654 the master Francesco Dotti and the architect Francesco Martini modified the whole structure by building a deep apse and a square antechamber with a decorated vault and a dome. The painters Mitelli and Colonna were asked to decorate the chapel; they finished the work in 1657. During Dotti's refurbishing of the whole church (1727–1737) the chapel was partially changed, mainly in the liturgical apparel.

fd7ea3bd-87be-5e84-a68b-74d44c3f3fc9.name: Tomb
fd7ea3bd-87be-5e84-a68b-74d44c3f3fc9.description:
The tomb, which is made of gilded silver shaped like a reliquary, holds a casket within which a figurine of Christ lies. Resting upon a trilateral base and supported on the backs of three ivory dragons, the tomb is decorated with embossed and chased foliate and *rocaille* ornaments and jewels. Enamel tablets hold within them scenes from the Life of Christ. From the base, a halo rises surrounded by a border of double rays. Attached to the base are allegorical figures of Faith, Hope and Love, flanked by St. Peter and St. Paul, and above them the figures of the Fathers of the Church Saints Augustine, Ambrose, Jerome and Gregory. The centre of the sunburst halo holds an enamelled painting of the Virgin and Child in a jewelled frame. It is decorated with foliate and *rocaille* ornaments, supported by two gilded angels. Above the frame is a splendid jewelled crown with a pendant pearl, flanked by two small ivory angels.  
Made in Augsburg and bought for the treasury with money bequeathed by Cardinal Juraj Haulik (the first Archbishop of Zagreb enthroned in 1853) a great patron of the arts and patriot whose ideas reflected the Enlightenment spirit.
fd7ea3bd-87be-5e84-a68b-74d44c3f3fc9.short_description: A gilded silver tomb shaped like a reliquary, which holds a casket within which a figurine of Christ lies. It rests upon a trilateral base supported on the backs of three ivory dragons. The tomb is decorated with embossed and chased foliate and *rocaille* ornaments and jewels. Enamelled tablets hold within them scenes from the Life of Christ.

fd93f758-39d0-53bd-b0d1-b105ee918d94.name: *Trompe l’œil* with Pious Pictures of *St. Philipp* and the *Virgin Mary*
fd93f758-39d0-53bd-b0d1-b105ee918d94.description:
Elias Mögel was active in Pozsony (Bratislava). His family background is unknown; the first piece of information about him is his wedding in 1751. His last will and testament was written in 1779 and announced on 12 June 1786. His earliest, signed, still life dates from 1760, the latest from 1784. Mögel would have known the Swiss branch of *trompe l'œil* painting through the circle of Johann Gaspar Füssli (1706–1782). The Quodlibets of the writer and professor of drawing in Zürich already carry an unmistakable intention of a popular and artistic education; all that might be of interest to one wanting to appreciate art seems to be present in this picture and its pair: etchings and engravings of all possible techniques, paintings, different types of paper and materials find their place on a trimmed piece of illusionistically painted wood.  
Mögel's paintings served in the improvement of general taste while also evoking a pious disposition. The illusory painting creates a milieu for the depiction of the saints and thus the printed pious paper-pictures, having been popular since the Middle Ages, were advanced here to works of art while at the same time they continue a century-long tradition of religious still life painting. The pair of this painting, conserved in the Bishop's Palace in Vác, is a *trompe l'œil* with engraved pictures of *St. Barbara* and *Salvator Mundi* (after Piazzetta) fixed with an iron nail, and accompanied by a paper with text referring to the Saint.  
Mögel also painted profane *trompe l'œil* pictures and imitated the Dutch genre painters as well. His signed picture kept in the Xantus János Museum in Győr was inspired by Rembrandt's pupil, Frans Bol; his two small genre scenes in Sopron were modelled on Gottfried Schalcken's works. The scenes of the Card players and Pipe smokers in Andrássy Castle in Krasznahorka (Krásna Hôrka) are reminiscent of Adriaen Brower's pictures. A series of six character-head studies, also kept there, may be attributed to him conditionally, as can the *trompe l'œil* of a collector's cabinet in the Museum of Červený Kameň.
fd93f758-39d0-53bd-b0d1-b105ee918d94.short_description: Mögel, who worked in Pozsony (Bratislava), was a master of *trompe l'œil*. This work together with its pair imitated engravings representing pious paper-pictures that had been popular since the Middle Ages.
fd93f758-39d0-53bd-b0d1-b105ee918d94.holder: Bishop’s Palace (Museum of the Diocese) in Vác
fd93f758-39d0-53bd-b0d1-b105ee918d94.method_for_datation: Signed lower right: Elias Mögel pinxit 1773
fd93f758-39d0-53bd-b0d1-b105ee918d94.bibliography:
Mojzer, M., (ed) *The Metamorphosis of Themes: Secular Subjects in the Art of the Baroque in Central Europe,* exhibition catalogue, Budapest, 1993, p. 397.  
Petrová-Pleskotová, A. “K životu a dielu maliara Eliasa Mögela”, *Ars,* 1998, 1–3, pp. 202–213.
keywords: Madonna; St. Barbara; Salvator Mundi; Johann Gaspar Füssli; Piazzetta; Rembrandt; Frans Bol; Gottfried Schalcken; Adriaen Brower; Count Andrássy; Elias Mögel; Pozsony; Pressburg; Vác; popular art; devotional painting; devotional print
fd93f758-39d0-53bd-b0d1-b105ee918d94.author: Anna Jávor

fdd61291-e9d2-50e6-9078-b7370d4dec42.name: Pilgrimage Church of the Scourged Saviour "in der Wies"  ("in the meadow")
fdd61291-e9d2-50e6-9078-b7370d4dec42.description: Embedded in the hilly landscape at the foot of a mountain named Trauchberg, the ensemble is comprised of the church building as well as the U-shaped priory building abutting the chancel. The latter served as living quarters for priests, pilgrim hospice and at the same time, as a summer residence of the abbot of Steingaden. The lay church, arranged in an oval central-plan with an interior processional ambulatory, connects to the chancel which is decorated with gilded Rocaille stucco and brightly coloured imitation of marble and is accompanied by galleries for noble persons. The two-storey pilgrimage altar soars in the chancel, integrated into the column architecture of the galleries. The arcaded zone of the predominantly frescoed vaults is decorated with a fully mature Rocaille stucco. This ornamental structure also forms the arches and windows of the architecture in a unique way which is due to the wooden construction of the vaults. This allows the vaults  to exhaust all rational rules to the extent that the arches in the chancel appear to sag in a statically absurd manner.
fdd61291-e9d2-50e6-9078-b7370d4dec42.short_description: With the so-called Wieskirche, embedded in the hilly landscape of upper Bavarian Alpine upland, the famous church builder and stuccoer Dominikus Zimmermann not only created a major work, but also the Rococo church par excellence, by capriciously making the light-filled architecture subject to the virtuous Rocaille stucco. Additionally, the vaults are decorated with delicately coloured frescoes done by the hand of his brother Johann Baptist.
fdd61291-e9d2-50e6-9078-b7370d4dec42.bibliography:
Bauer, H. and Rupprecht, B. (eds), *Corpus der barocken Deckenmalerei in Deutschland, Vol. 1: Freistaat Bayern, Regierungsbezirk Oberbayern. Die Landkreise Landsberg am Lech – Starnberg – Weilheim-Schongau*, Munich: Süddeutscher Verlag, 1976: 600–623.  
Harries, K., *The Bavarian Rococo Church: Between Faith and Aestheticism*, New Haven/London: Yale University Press, 1983: 94, 139–144.  
Hitchcock, Henry-Russell, *German Rococo: The Zimmermann Brothers*, London: Penguin, 1968: 68–78, 91, 94.  
Petzet, M. (ed), *Die Wies: Geschichte und Restaurierung* (Arbeitshefte des Bayerischen Landesamtes für Denkmalpflege 55), Munich: Lipp, 1992.  
Pörnbacher, H., *Die Wies: Wallfahrtskirche zum gegeißelten Heiland* (Kleine Kunstführer 1), 23rd revised edition, Regensburg: Schnell & Steiner, 2002.
fdd61291-e9d2-50e6-9078-b7370d4dec42.history: The reason for construction was a miraculous weeping of a processional statue embodying the Scourged Saviour, which is supposed to have taken place in the seclusion of Wies on 14 June 1738. As a result, the nearby Premonstratensian Abbey of Steingaden built a Chapel of Mercy which soon became too small because of the increased flux of pilgrims. Therefore, the architect and stuccoer Dominikus Zimmermann was commissioned to construct a spacious church. After the laying of the foundation stone on 10 July 1746, construction was staged in two phases. The first phase, up to 1749, was the chancel building, alone also functioning as a new Chapel of Mercy, together with the abutting priory building. Next was the lay church, designed as a central building, which was able to be consecrated on 1 September 1754.
fdd61291-e9d2-50e6-9078-b7370d4dec42.patrons: Marian Mayr (gov. 1745–72) Abbot of the Premonstratensian Abbey of Steingaden
fdd61291-e9d2-50e6-9078-b7370d4dec42.author: Peter Heinrich Jahn

02670817-41d7-5797-a20d-2808406b0faa.name: *St. Jacob before God as intercessor for Innsbruck, Tyrol, the Diocese of Brixen and Austria*
02670817-41d7-5797-a20d-2808406b0faa.description: The fresco cycle from Cosmas Damian Asam has the work of the church’s patron saint as its theme. Asam painted illusionistic architecture in the shallow cupolas, a task which he solved differently in each scene. There are no references to real built architecture. In the centre of the perspectively exaggerated depiction a statue of the apostle can be seen. Supplicants from all estates are gathered around him, while Jacob implores God for heavenly assistance.
02670817-41d7-5797-a20d-2808406b0faa.artist: Cosmas Damian Asam (1686–1739); Egid Quirin Asam (1692–1750)

040b2846-3c5d-576f-85cf-a8f925d606cd.name: Virgin Mary with Child Handing the Order Gown to St. Norbert in the Presence of St. Augustine
040b2846-3c5d-576f-85cf-a8f925d606cd.description: This side altar altarpiece is typical of Leicher, Maulbertsch’s associate and frequent collaborator. The layout, colour scheme and movements of the figures in an S-shaped composition, reflect Maulbertsch’s expressive style although transposed to a softer, more lyrical outcome. The presence of St. Norbert, founder of the Premonstratensian order, refers to the “mother” monastery in Louka. The subject of the picture is the vision of St. Norbert in Prémontré when he saw the Virgin Mary, who gave her blessing to his intention to establish a monastery there, and handed him a white monastic gown.
040b2846-3c5d-576f-85cf-a8f925d606cd.location: Pilgrimage Church of the Scourged Saviour, Dyje, side altar

059edbc5-9442-564e-ae32-2efb3b02e0ba.name: Benediction Room
059edbc5-9442-564e-ae32-2efb3b02e0ba.description:
The Benediction Room at the centre of the royal palace appears to be part of the Basilica as it has the same polychrome marble decoration.  
It symbolises the divine origins of Absolute Kingship, to whose authority even the Church submitted. From this room over the Basilica, the Royal Family attended mass, and from the veranda (on the opposite side) opening onto the square, King João V blessed his subjects.
059edbc5-9442-564e-ae32-2efb3b02e0ba.location: In the middle of the Royal Palace

0952e239-ee28-5d99-b908-2b46023f7747.name: High altar
0952e239-ee28-5d99-b908-2b46023f7747.description: The sculpted, distinctly vertical altar, symbolically shaped like a tongue, is placed within a tall arcade that reaches to the gallery on the second floor. Unlike many other constructions of its kind it does not dominate the church interior but symbolically enhances it. There is no ornamental decoration or painting.
