The building itself, created by matter and the work of light in space, is the sole bearer of meaning. Light is also symbolically divided in the space. In the bottom section the area is illuminated by candles, i.e. fire an earthly light, while on the first floor Divine Light enters the space through mirrors. The symbolic linking and oscillation of rays of light is portrayed in the ribbed walls of the first floor. The second floor and the top of the vaulting, where a symbol of the saint (epitomising a holy miracle) is found instead of the usual symbol of the Holy Spirit, are illuminated by pure light coming through the windows. Without a doubt this horizontal three-part approach also symbolises the Holy Trinity.

0a72386e-7c5f-545b-9709-c7b0eb095d20.name: *The Creation of Adam*
0a72386e-7c5f-545b-9709-c7b0eb095d20.description: The first story of the cycle, to the left of the entrance represents the Creation of Man as the highest gesture of love of God.

0ae494ef-cd06-5be1-a894-e8f72b874300.name: Holy Trinity Column
0ae494ef-cd06-5be1-a894-e8f72b874300.description: A hexagonal stepped base carries a trilateral concave pedestal the columns of which support a sculpture of God the Father, Christ in heaven, and a pyramid crowned with the symbol of the Holy Spirit on a radial halo. The statues of the Immaculata and the saints are by the court sculptor, Lengelacher, after the painter, A. J. Prenner. The bottom section features allegories of Love, Faith and Hope, and emblems of the patrons.
0ae494ef-cd06-5be1-a894-e8f72b874300.artist: Anton Josef Prenner (1683 Wallerstein – 1761 Wien) – Ignaz Lengelacher (1698 Unter Peissenberg – 1780 Baden)

0d11fd1e-2845-5a2d-9be0-10b44ca4b3ea.name: View of the exterior
0d11fd1e-2845-5a2d-9be0-10b44ca4b3ea.description: The most significant features of the church, in its picturesque location near the river Inn, are the ridge turret above the choir and the tail gable on the front façade, as well as the skylight turret with onion dome above the crossing. The portal from red marble bears the inscription 1764.
0d11fd1e-2845-5a2d-9be0-10b44ca4b3ea.artist: Franz de Paula Penz (1707–1772); Christoph Anton Mayr (c. 1720–1771)

1174b2ab-da5e-56fc-b6bc-cc3311897b6b.name: Mount of Olives
1174b2ab-da5e-56fc-b6bc-cc3311897b6b.description: Behind the high altar is a grotto, “the Garden of Gethsemane”, with a relief sculpture of Christ and the Apostles on the Mount of Olives before Christ was tortured. A group of sinners suffering in purgatory are depicted on a tomb to accentuate His role as Saviour.
1174b2ab-da5e-56fc-b6bc-cc3311897b6b.location: High altar, Pilgrimage Church of the Elevation of the Holy Cross, Jaroměřice u Jevíčka

130a251d-cd8c-55de-81ca-2e58a7733c0b.name: St. Gregory
130a251d-cd8c-55de-81ca-2e58a7733c0b.description: Illusionary architecture and ornamentation make up a major part of the church decoration. They also provide a background for one of the Church Fathers in a vault joint. St. Gregory is a crypto-portrait of his namesake, Řehoř Lambeck, a benefactor of the church and art-loving abbot of Louka Monastery. J. Winterhalder Jr., a pupil and close associate of Maulbertsch, participated in the painting of the Church Fathers, Prophets and Evangelists.
130a251d-cd8c-55de-81ca-2e58a7733c0b.location: Pilgrimage Church of the Scourged Saviour, Dyje, detail of the Fresco
130a251d-cd8c-55de-81ca-2e58a7733c0b.artist: Franz Anton Maulbertsch (1724 Langenargen am Bodensee – 1796 Vienna) – Josef Winterhalder Jr. (1743 Vöhrenbach – 1807 Znojmo)

14756176-c5ce-547a-a93a-d0113a7e9513.name: General View of the Nave towards the Chancel
14756176-c5ce-547a-a93a-d0113a7e9513.description: Although small and low, the true value of the church interior lies in the densely carved and gilded woodwork of the lateral altarpieces, seen most spectacularly in the chancel.
14756176-c5ce-547a-a93a-d0113a7e9513.location: Interior, Sanctuary of Bom Jesus de Matosinhos
14756176-c5ce-547a-a93a-d0113a7e9513.artist: Portuguese woodcarvers: Luís Pereira da Costa (active 1724–?), Domingos Martins Moreira (active 1746–1750)

15a87fb6-8298-5ff6-a114-ee8cde8ea202.name: Pulpit
15a87fb6-8298-5ff6-a114-ee8cde8ea202.description: A beautiful example of an Early Classicist pulpit in austere forms virtually without ornamentation or pictorial programme. Instead of Baroque rhetoric—which was no longer expected of the preacher—the pulpit was designed to provide a dignified frame for an edifying sermon. The design originates from Hagenauer and Nesselthaler and was executed by Peter Pflauder, a stucco mason and altar carpenter from Thannheim in Tyrol.

192646de-9480-5ec8-a969-8316a9ee6e28.name: Abbot Loge
192646de-9480-5ec8-a969-8316a9ee6e28.description: The more modest, although no less virtuously modelled and decorated, counterpart to the pulpit forms the loge of the abbot of Steingaden.
192646de-9480-5ec8-a969-8316a9ee6e28.location: Lay church, column pair right of the chancel
192646de-9480-5ec8-a969-8316a9ee6e28.artist: Design: Dominikus Zimmermann (1685–1766) Execution: Pontian Steinhauser (1688–1755)

1991c012-f312-5724-ad34-6745f6148321.name: Angels
1991c012-f312-5724-ad34-6745f6148321.description: The decoration in the chapel originally consisted only of this group of sculpted angels bearing a celestial sphere decorated with five stars and with St. John of Nepomuk standing on top of it. The statues were created by local artists.

1c18232c-3877-5f00-a0b7-461e6bf058e6.name: Interior opposite the choir
1c18232c-3877-5f00-a0b7-461e6bf058e6.description: The effect generated by the interior in the ideal view from the west is determined by the massive pilasters, which form the support for the pristine semi-circular spans of the double transverse and single longitudinal arches. Their arrangement generates, as is usual for pilaster churches, a coulisse-like prospect, however the room is so short due to the sequence of only three elements (two nave bays and choir) that it almost has the appearance of a central-plan building. The high altar with the miraculous picture, which is situated free-standing in the middle of the choir, thus appears, not as a distant goal, but as quasi the centre of the spatial sequence, especially as the grandeur of its ciborium echoes the four-arched structure of the two-nave bays.

1c762e1a-46e3-5876-b435-e216529f8c0d.name: The Bells of Lisbon and the Sanctus Singing Angel
1c762e1a-46e3-5876-b435-e216529f8c0d.description: Two small frescoes refer to the canonisation of St. Anthony in 1232. The angels invoking him represent the heavenly participation in the pontificial act, while the bells refer to a miracle that occurred at the same time: all of the church bells in Lisbon, hometown of the saint, chimed simultaneously without human involvement. The virtuosic view from below and especially the realism of the bell cage give these images the status of pictorial showpieces.
1c762e1a-46e3-5876-b435-e216529f8c0d.location: Vault of the spandrel spaces between the octagonal and the oval structure

1d50e49c-ec78-5964-9727-5f82a4990f66.name: Exterior
1d50e49c-ec78-5964-9727-5f82a4990f66.description: Only the curved windows, of a bell-shape on the nave, indicate a building of the Late Baroque period. Everything else is of unimposing design and the former Gothic buttresses have been reduced to bands. The west side has not been designed as an ornamental façade and the gable has even been finished in shingles. The shaft of the Gothic tower with pointed helm roof has remained unrendered.

1e3ded35-5fc2-5f5f-b377-ddc4c0c909a6.name: Stucco
1e3ded35-5fc2-5f5f-b377-ddc4c0c909a6.description: The stuccowork was crafted by one of the great masters of the stucco school  in Wessobrunn, where the central themes were snail and shell ornaments. He combined those with traditional motifs from the Early Baroque stucco art in Munich, particularly laurel branches, herms of angels, and strips of stuccowork framing geometrically configured sections. The single motifs are mostly cast with wooden moulds.
1e3ded35-5fc2-5f5f-b377-ddc4c0c909a6.artist: Design: Konstantin Pader; Execution: Matthias II Schmuzer

1ecaa6cc-9678-575c-974d-6bc822ccfe3c.name: *Sala terrena*
1ecaa6cc-9678-575c-974d-6bc822ccfe3c.description: The hall by the passageway to the garden features a segmented vault. It is decorated, like the chateau floors, with stuccowork containing “mirrors” filled with painted scenes from Ovid's *Metamorphoses*, figures of gods and muses.

1f6a275f-c79d-5523-8152-e66ee749a6b7.name: Façade
1f6a275f-c79d-5523-8152-e66ee749a6b7.description: The double-tower façade of St. Jacob is a Late Baroque interpretation of a basic plan based on the Salzburg Dome. The projecting towers – which form a unit with the two-storey middle section – are characteristic. In contrast to Salzburg the transitions are more fluent, employing concave wall sections. The vertical oval windows of the upper storeys establish a number of thematic accents. The towers’ upper storeys are also more powerfully built than in Salzburg.
1f6a275f-c79d-5523-8152-e66ee749a6b7.artist: Johann Jakob Herkomer (1648–1717); Johann Georg Fischer (1673–1747)

1fd944dc-83c6-5e83-8dba-701c2a61c3e2.name: *Death of the Virgin* (smaller central medallion)
1fd944dc-83c6-5e83-8dba-701c2a61c3e2.description: Small octagonal medallion showing a representation of the Death of the Virgin inspired by the mannerist engravings of Adrien Collaert and Cornelis Galle.
1fd944dc-83c6-5e83-8dba-701c2a61c3e2.artist: António de Oliveira Bernardes (1662–1732) and Pedro Figueira [n.d.]

224f5f0e-a3d6-5685-8342-9a71082c79cc.name: Ground plan
224f5f0e-a3d6-5685-8342-9a71082c79cc.description: The principal compositional element is a five-pointed star (five-pointed ground plan, five entrances, five altar niches, ten chapels surrounding the central space, five stars and five angels on the high altar), symbolising the five wounds of Christ, five letters in the Latin word *tacui* (“I was silent”) and, in particular, five stars in the halo of St. John of Nepomuk. Legend has it that the stars appeared in the River Vltava after the martyr had been drowned in it.

25b397ce-e589-53c6-b2f5-884c9b6d6745.name: Chapel of St. Pauline
25b397ce-e589-53c6-b2f5-884c9b6d6745.description: Andrýsek’s original chapel stood until 1677 but was pulled down during the course of the construction of the new church. The frescos commemorate the origins of the pilgrimage site. The altarpiece represents the Olomouc patroness whose remains were donated to the Olomouc Jesuits by Pope Gregory XV in 1623. The procession held as part of the transfer of the relics was said to have thwarted the plague.
25b397ce-e589-53c6-b2f5-884c9b6d6745.artist: Paul Troger (1698 Zell, near Welsberg – 1762 Vienna)

25d59ad7-f146-5a66-b99c-640d389ce20d.name: Altar of St. Barbara
25d59ad7-f146-5a66-b99c-640d389ce20d.description: Like its match, the Altar of St. Joseph, it is framed with a *trompe\-l'œil* painting of luxurious drapery rather than architectural elements. The role of the structural parts, overtaken by decorative and figural motifs such as volutes and *putti*, makes for the altar's picturesque and extremely dynamic sculptural programme.
25d59ad7-f146-5a66-b99c-640d389ce20d.location: Along the southern side of the triumphal arch, Parish Church of Our Lady of the Snow

25ede1f2-8f70-5252-9d21-3b21a63183bf.name: The Apostle Peter
25ede1f2-8f70-5252-9d21-3b21a63183bf.description: The bust, in relief of the Apostle Peter, opens onto the entrance of the chapel with six reliefs – originally gilded – of Old Testament scenes featuring motifs of sacrifice and thanksgiving by the same sculptor. Sattler also collaborated with V. Render on the Olomouc fountains.

261d6cf2-f4d5-5ea8-a4c4-7c1fe310d8d9.name: Library
261d6cf2-f4d5-5ea8-a4c4-7c1fe310d8d9.description: The library equipment was enabled by a generous donation from Baron Trenck who is mummified in the monastery crypt. The ceiling painting represents John Bonaventura showing a crucifix to Thomas Aquinas in response to a query as to the origin of the sources of his writings. One remarkable item is a human skeleton in a display case amidst the other library cases. The skeleton was used for anatomy studies and also symbolised, within the library iconography, a *memento mori*.
261d6cf2-f4d5-5ea8-a4c4-7c1fe310d8d9.location: Capuchin Monastery and the Church of the Invention of the Holy Cross, Brno
261d6cf2-f4d5-5ea8-a4c4-7c1fe310d8d9.artist: Josef Stern (1716 Graz – 1775 Brno), Ondřej Schweigl (1735–1812 Brno)

26371767-cb3f-5ce5-9d43-eccf210c490a.name: Collateral Altarpiece
26371767-cb3f-5ce5-9d43-eccf210c490a.description: Both collateral altarpieces are very similar, made of gilt carved wood  and flanked by pilasters decorated with acanthus leaves.
26371767-cb3f-5ce5-9d43-eccf210c490a.location: Church interior, Sanctuary of Our Lady of Good Remedy
26371767-cb3f-5ce5-9d43-eccf210c490a.artist: Frei José de Santo António Ferreira (active1764-66)

272076e8-33b2-5acd-b85d-2a9e6720b295.name: Child Jesus teaching the Virgin
272076e8-33b2-5acd-b85d-2a9e6720b295.description: Focusing on their lesson, Jesus and Mary appear to be engaged in a private interaction but are welcoming the viewer to join them.
272076e8-33b2-5acd-b85d-2a9e6720b295.artist: António de Oliveira Bernardes (1662–1732) and Pedro Figueira [n.d.]

2a8f2ad2-0175-5d0b-b8ba-1b55369ff2d5.name: Façade
2a8f2ad2-0175-5d0b-b8ba-1b55369ff2d5.description: The façade, with its two lightly projecting towers framing the two-storey central section structured in three vertical axes with tail gable, is a later successor to Salzburg Cathedral. However, they are quite different in character – the Early Baroque model appears considerably bulkier and more austere, the Early Classicist successor more two-dimensional and with finer proportions and structure.

2dabfc2d-d0c7-5629-b60d-d85fe2d540f8.name: *The Coronation of the Virgin*
2dabfc2d-d0c7-5629-b60d-d85fe2d540f8.description: Above the frieze decorated with many golden stuccoes opens the dome, decorated with semi columns and rosettes. The open sky frames the Virgin as she is lifted to heaven to be crowned by the angels. The complex spatial articulation along with the violently vertical scene and the rapid succession of grounds achieves perfect foreshortening, a good example of the high level of Mitelli and Colonna’s achievements in decorative painting. The two painters are perfectly at ease working together so it is practically impossible to tell the different hands.
2dabfc2d-d0c7-5629-b60d-d85fe2d540f8.location: Dome of the square antechamber of the chapel of the Rosary, Basilica di San Domenico, Bologna
2dabfc2d-d0c7-5629-b60d-d85fe2d540f8.artist: Angelo Michele Colonna and Agostino Mitelli

2e551a44-ed15-554e-b118-1f8beb1b9f7d.name: The Virgin Mary of Old Brno
2e551a44-ed15-554e-b118-1f8beb1b9f7d.description: This picture of the Virgin Mary is named after its second location. It was the palladium of Brno, a miraculous picture (Thaumaturga) of the Madonna and Child donated to the Augustinian Monastery in Brno by Emperor Charles IV. Members of major Moravian aristocratic families were traditionally wedded before the Thaumaturga. The reliquary, originally embedded in the child’s heart, makes up the clasp of the Madonna’s dress. Relief letters, gilded crowns with precious stones, and a chain come from the period of the picture’s coronation and its incorporation into the new altar. The image was credited with the salvation of Brno from the Swedish siege at the end of the Thirty Years’ War, as well as with healing properties and other miracles.

31788a7e-54f2-5c5b-8dda-c0fc298370ec.name: Side Chapel, left (Holy Sacrament Chapel)
31788a7e-54f2-5c5b-8dda-c0fc298370ec.location: Interior, Sanctuary of Bom Jesus de Matosinhos
31788a7e-54f2-5c5b-8dda-c0fc298370ec.artist: Portuguese woodcarvers: Luís Pereira da Costa (active 1724–?), Domingos Martins Moreira (active 1746–1750)

33bda0f2-7ee5-5ec5-a93c-d5ad872cb9d3.name: Mausoleum for Archduke Maximilian III, the German Master
33bda0f2-7ee5-5ec5-a93c-d5ad872cb9d3.description: The bronze mausoleum, part of the inventory of the previous building, was designed by Hubert Gerhart from Munich and was completed by Caspar Gras of Innsbruck. It is one of the most important early Baroque mausoleums, with lifelike expressiveness, above all in the depiction of the Archduke who was Grand Master of the German Order of Knights, and St. George, the order’s patron saint. The superstructure is formed of four spiral columns ranked with vines, populated by all manner of animals.
33bda0f2-7ee5-5ec5-a93c-d5ad872cb9d3.location: Left transept apse, St. Jacob’s Cathedral
33bda0f2-7ee5-5ec5-a93c-d5ad872cb9d3.artist: Hubert Gerhard (c. 1545–1623); Caspar Gras (1585–1674); Heinrich Reinhart (1575–1629)

34bb86f6-37dc-5242-9419-abe2436ed8e4.name: Stairway (general view)
34bb86f6-37dc-5242-9419-abe2436ed8e4.description: The design for the staircase was drawn up in 1777. Building began in 1781 and continued until 1969.
34bb86f6-37dc-5242-9419-abe2436ed8e4.location: Exterior, Sanctuary of Our Lady of Good Remedy

3636a025-d6fb-5112-aadf-5dc2f03d7988.name: Parish Church of the Assumption of the Virgin Mary
3636a025-d6fb-5112-aadf-5dc2f03d7988.description: F. A. Rottal recruited leading artists in his services. The high altar does not feature an altarpiece but, instead, there is a sculpture of the Assumption of the Virgin Mary by J. J. Schauberger. The precious sculpted decoration of the church is complemented by a baptismal font by O. Zahner with a sculpture of Christ’s Baptism on Earth, and side altars and statues on the frontage. The sculptors joined forces in other commissions also.
3636a025-d6fb-5112-aadf-5dc2f03d7988.artist: Filiberto Luchese (1606, Melide – 1666, Vienna), Jan Jiří Schauberger (?, before 1725 Vienna, active in Olomouc – 1744 Brno), Ondřej Zahner (1709 Ettershausen – 1752 Olomouc)

38f8230e-0728-5617-bd21-ae2887da3089.name: St. John of Nepomuk
38f8230e-0728-5617-bd21-ae2887da3089.description: St. John of Nepomuk was a popular saint frequently considered protector of roads and particularly bridges, marking the manner of his death. He was thrown in the Vltava from Charles Bridge in 1393. One obvious difference between the statues by Jelínek and Winterhalder is the relief-segmented cloak, which creates movement and disturbance in order to stir the viewer’s emotions.

3a82940b-0422-54ce-94e9-7b0610d5dd16.name: Cupola
3a82940b-0422-54ce-94e9-7b0610d5dd16.description: This was the first cupola built in Portugal, similar to that of St. Peter’s in Rome. Sixty-two metres high, it is marble outside and with polychrome marble inside. The cupola has an eight-sided form and eight windows, above which are the sculpted litanies of the Virgin Mary. Forty-one men worked simultaneously on the decoration “very well and at ease”, according to a testimony in contemporary sources.

3f371b7c-e6f8-56ea-ad51-4698c54c3ba9.name: St. Barbara
3f371b7c-e6f8-56ea-ad51-4698c54c3ba9.description: In the 1760s the altars were supplemented with predella paintings by J. Jablonský, who settled in Brno. In the final phase of works he echoed painters from the Vienna Academy circle, collaborating with the artist, J. Stern.
3f371b7c-e6f8-56ea-ad51-4698c54c3ba9.location: Pilgrimage Church of the Virgin Mary of Dolours, Side altar
3f371b7c-e6f8-56ea-ad51-4698c54c3ba9.artist: Johann Jablonský (1737 Rychnov nad Kněžnou – after 1774 Brno?)

4245f4f1-ced8-58b2-8737-09920f72fa22.name: Interior
4245f4f1-ced8-58b2-8737-09920f72fa22.description: General view of the interior of the church. There is a huge representation of Calvary with life-size figures at the main altar.
4245f4f1-ced8-58b2-8737-09920f72fa22.location: Bom Jesus Church, Bom Jesus de Braga Sanctuary (Bom Jesus do Monte)

42f3e619-7f2e-5807-987f-322644ef856c.name: High altar
42f3e619-7f2e-5807-987f-322644ef856c.description: The architect of the church, Konstantin Pader, also provided designs for the stucco and the altars, which creates homogeneity of both structure and decoration. The high altar is characterised by an enhanced plasticity of its elements and can be attributed to the High Baroque. The imitating ebony and marble colour scheme and gold-plated ornamental applications were typical of that era. The altarpiece, framed by an aedicula attached to a tall pedestal, depicts Christ's Deposition from the Cross and therefore conveys the biblical scene necessary for the interpretation of the miraculous image. Beneath is an opening that allows the visitor to glance at the miraculous pietà and the remains of the pear tree trunk.
42f3e619-7f2e-5807-987f-322644ef856c.artist: Design: Konstantin Pader; Altarpiece: Johann Hehrl

4362690b-8bce-5978-8be2-ef7d62b6ca6f.name: Memory Hermitage
4362690b-8bce-5978-8be2-ef7d62b6ca6f.description: The small Hermitage is isolated. It is quadrangular in shape with a reverse ogee dome crowned with a rounded pinnacle. Despite its popularity it is very difficult to define the Memory Hermitage in chronological terms. Its “cubic” form and bulbous dome undoubtedly remind us of the ancient Muslim *qubba.*

4460d659-be3c-5edc-a835-cb31775cb892.name: Façade
4460d659-be3c-5edc-a835-cb31775cb892.description: Despite the dominant horizontal façade, the two towers are thin and crowned with the reverse ogee pinnacles that are typical of regional Portuguese Baroque.

47ae5572-acbf-57a2-be11-0e35cf01e522.name: *The Glory of St. Ignatius of Loyola*
47ae5572-acbf-57a2-be11-0e35cf01e522.description: The glory of the founder saint of the Jesuits dominates the middle of the vault of the chapel. It is inspired by the great decoration with the same subject painted by Andrea Pozzo in Rome.
47ae5572-acbf-57a2-be11-0e35cf01e522.location: Chapel of the Jesuit novitiate, vault

483269b7-dbdb-5903-9179-333113251b69.name: High altar
483269b7-dbdb-5903-9179-333113251b69.description: The high altar in front of the choir wall in the southern cross arm with columns in bright coloured stucco marble and white figural decoration is the work of an unknown master craftsman. The venerated miraculous crucifix has been inserted in place of an altarpiece, a work of the 17th century.
483269b7-dbdb-5903-9179-333113251b69.location: Choir (southern cross arm), Catholic Pilgrimage Church of the Holy Cross

4ad97887-f621-598c-8c7f-52693a816738.name: St. Felix of Cantalice
4ad97887-f621-598c-8c7f-52693a816738.description: The entrance of the church, in sloping terrain, was adjusted by a terrace with statues of Capuchin saints. The sculptor, who trained in the Rhine Basin region, worked in the Brno workshop of J. J. Schauberger. His compact figures are noteworthy for their expressive faces.
4ad97887-f621-598c-8c7f-52693a816738.location: Capuchin Monastery and the Church of the Invention of the Holy Cross, Brno

4b13da99-6999-503a-b4bc-3a583fb6e0dc.name: Altar of the Holy Cross
4b13da99-6999-503a-b4bc-3a583fb6e0dc.description: The three parts of the Holy Cross altar embody the sanctuary of the pilgrimage. Within elaborate niches of stucco marble on the corners of the choir arch, one finds the assistant figures of the central crucifix: the miraculous *Mater Dolorosa* on the left-hand side, and on the right, the *Apostle St. John*. The gilded *rocaille* elements, as well as the many different and lively putti, are considered masterpieces of Üblher.
4b13da99-6999-503a-b4bc-3a583fb6e0dc.location: Choir and choir arch, Catholic Parish and Pilgrimage Church of the Exaltation of the Cross and Our Lady of Sorrows

4dec7c99-613e-59ef-83b0-ed79acbd070f.name: Monumental arch so called ‘del Meloncello’
4dec7c99-613e-59ef-83b0-ed79acbd070f.description: This ingenious structure links the side of the portico coming from the city to the one climbing up the hill, as a sort of overpass. The monumental arch was built under the direction of the same architect who designed the new church; he was probably charged with the building of a project by a great protagonist of the European baroque age, Francesco Galli, known as Bibiena, whose education as a theatre architect and stage designer influenced the general idea and the decorative features of the work.
4dec7c99-613e-59ef-83b0-ed79acbd070f.location: Exterior, Santuario della Beata Vergine di san Luca

4e21d747-872b-5b6e-941c-e4be1506d6b9.name: Pulpit
4e21d747-872b-5b6e-941c-e4be1506d6b9.description: Ornamental structures populated by cherubs as emissaries of the Heavenly Host overrun the foot of the pulpit and pile up on the sounding board. The Old Testament tablets of the Ten Commandments refer to the word of God as well as symbols of the four Latin Church Fathers to its theological interpretation. A boy riding a fish symbolises  the baptized soul as the recipient of the homily-conveyed messages of salvation.
4e21d747-872b-5b6e-941c-e4be1506d6b9.location: Lay church, column pair left of the chancel
4e21d747-872b-5b6e-941c-e4be1506d6b9.artist: Design: Dominikus Zimmermann (1685–1766) Execution: Pontian Steinhauser (1688–1755)

4e2c1b12-21c6-58e5-bf20-cdc0eb585033.name: Saints John and Paul
4e2c1b12-21c6-58e5-bf20-cdc0eb585033.description:
The side-altar painting commemorates the penultimate abbot of the Premonstratensian Monastery (and possibly also the creator of the complex iconography of the ceiling paintings) whose tomb lies in front of the altar. A picture of Roman martyrs, protectors from unfavourable weather, is framed by an altar by O. Schweigl. The function of the saints as the country’s protectors may also be understood symbolically: a 1772 decree considerably restricted the organisation of pilgrimages, while an imperial patent from 1783 prohibited them completely.  
The picture in the attachment is of St. Gilbert, the abbot’s favourite saint.

4fe53e71-5945-5d6a-9e28-e7a34d244285.name: Freemasons’ Room
4fe53e71-5945-5d6a-9e28-e7a34d244285.description: The decoration of the chateau was completed in the early 19th century, in the spirit of the “spiritual alchemy” of the late Enlightenment. The Mniszeks finished the Empire-style construction of the stable frontage and made minor Neo-Gothic and Romantic adjustments to the frontages. They also built chapels, crosses, obelisks and family memorials in the park. In 1816 Stanislav Mniszek purchased a stoneware factory and turned it into a famous manufactory.

50b56dcf-06cd-51c0-a478-2ba2d18b7a16.name: *St. George*
50b56dcf-06cd-51c0-a478-2ba2d18b7a16.description: The saint, shown as he transfixes the dragon writhing under his feet, along with the figure of St. Martin on the same altar, has similarities with the statues of Filip Jakob Straub on the High Altar of Welsche Kirche in Graz, which probably served Weinacht as an inspiration.
50b56dcf-06cd-51c0-a478-2ba2d18b7a16.location: Far-left intercolumniation of the High Altar, Parish Church of Our Lady of the Snow

5103c1d7-7cdc-5cd7-a8b3-15573cb52a74.name: Interior
5103c1d7-7cdc-5cd7-a8b3-15573cb52a74.description: In contrast to its plain exterior the building interior surprises with its ambitious combination of architecture and interior work and a magnificent prospect with the high altar at its centre. At the transition of the somewhat wider nave to the choir, projecting pilasters form the frame for the view in the direction of the altar. In the foreground rounded niches housing the side altars form the transition from nave to choir. Choir and niches form a triad at whose zenith the high altar with the Notburga shrine is staged like an oversized monstrance.
5103c1d7-7cdc-5cd7-a8b3-15573cb52a74.location: View from the nave into the choir

53a5bd73-a238-53c4-81c9-59518376497e.name: Coronation Monstrance
53a5bd73-a238-53c4-81c9-59518376497e.description: The radial monstrance is decorated with vine leaves and grapes, the Eucharist, symbol of Christ’s blood. Below the casket is a relief of the Madonna and Child; at the top, under a baldachin, is God and the dove of the Holy Spirit. Cartouches on the richly wrought pedestal feature paintings on enamel: the Madonna of Old Brno and half-figures of the order’s saints.

563c5781-e08e-5f36-b59b-bbc28044b3ab.name: View of Brno and the Premonstratensian Monastery in Zábrdovice
563c5781-e08e-5f36-b59b-bbc28044b3ab.description: The church galleries contain a number of votive pictures brought by pilgrims. This monumental canvas depicts the Brno Basin with the Zábrdovice Monastery which administered the pilgrimage site. The picture was donated by the canonry as an expression of thanks for the protection of Brno during the siege by Prussian and Saxon armies in 1742.

571b4393-48a0-5d36-b275-9a37e8ea9df6.name: Coronation Paraments
571b4393-48a0-5d36-b275-9a37e8ea9df6.description: Fabrics were essential elements of the coronation ceremony. Viennese embroiderers frequently worked for the monastery. In comparison with other preserved Paraments these appear rather poor. The most spectacular part of the coronation set was the altar with an altarpiece. Accompanying elements were subordinated to it through their reduced decorativeness.

58796dab-18c0-5c82-8173-c5e543e4c87a.name: Celebration of the Virgin Mary
58796dab-18c0-5c82-8173-c5e543e4c87a.description: The monumental fresco is by C. F. Sambach, a pupil of P. Troger and G. R. Donner and later a rector at the Vienna Academy. The central scene, placed in an illusionary architectural frame, is supplemented with allegories of the Virtues in pendentives. The bottom section features the coats of arms of the benefactors and angels spreading pilgrimage devotionalia from a cornucopia. Sambach also created the pictures for the side altars. This series of large paintings is among his best work.
58796dab-18c0-5c82-8173-c5e543e4c87a.location: Pilgrimage Church of the Virgin Mary of Dolours

5a414632-5957-5804-9e90-cd85d42a99f3.name: High Altar of the Church of St. Anne
5a414632-5957-5804-9e90-cd85d42a99f3.description: F. A. Rottal was a prominent investor. He built and restored churches (Hostýn) in his demesne, founded a Trinitarian Monastery in Holešov and reconstructed the Church of St. Anne. A lesser-known artist, J. F. Pilz’s paintings were a tour de force.
5a414632-5957-5804-9e90-cd85d42a99f3.artist: Ondřej Zahner (1709 Ettershausen – 1752 Olomouc), František Antonín Palko (1717 Breslau – 1767 Vienna)

5b042fed-0778-5fb0-9fbd-bea71502dbf8.name: High altar
5b042fed-0778-5fb0-9fbd-bea71502dbf8.description: The high altar in the form of a freestanding, four-columned ciborium is the work of Franz Karl Fischer, the son of the master builder Johann Georg Fischer of the Füssen school. The altar, in which in all likelihood the four columns of its predecessor from 1728 have been integrated, was designed by Joseph Stapf.  The columns are arranged in a trapezoid form, whereby the two rear columns frame the mensa with tabernacle, and form the rear wall of the structure. Above the tabernacle is a miraculous picture in an aureole, a Gothic Madonna with child. According to records a picture of the Virgin Mary was displayed under four columns in Wilton as early as 1311. The two angel candelabra which flank the altar are works of the late 17th century, presumably from Andreas Faistenberger.

5bc76a0c-5131-5c24-99d0-666fd90caf59.name: Allegory of Salvation
5bc76a0c-5131-5c24-99d0-666fd90caf59.description: The middle section of the vault is the centre of the longitudinal building and the principal part of its iconography. Adam and Eve embody the burden of eternal sin and mortality. Archangel Gabriel wreathed in flower garlands bears the Divine message of the salvation of mankind – the birth of Christ and his sacrifice – symbolised by a cross and the marks of Christ’s torture. The scene of the Supreme Divine Secret – where the Word becomes the body – closes with Archangel Michael weighing souls on Judgement Day. The arrival of the Saviour as foretold by the prophets is represented in the joints of the vault with Moses, Abraham, Noah and Enoch.
5bc76a0c-5131-5c24-99d0-666fd90caf59.location: Pilgrimage Church of the Scourged Saviour, Dyje, detail of the Fresco
5bc76a0c-5131-5c24-99d0-666fd90caf59.artist: Franz Anton Maulbertsch (1724 Langenargen am Bodensee – 1796 Vienna)

5bf676b7-c1ac-53ed-8e80-eafc74f0d3c4.name: The portico
5bf676b7-c1ac-53ed-8e80-eafc74f0d3c4.description: The construction of the long and sinuous portico in its actual shape started in 1674, thanks to the contributions of religious orders, noble families, guilds and private citizens. The project, made by Camillo Saccenti (already presented in 1655 but at that time thought to be too expensive) was modified by the architect Gian Giacomo Monti at the beginning of the eighteenth-century.  Based on the advice provided by the archbishop’s architect Giovanni Antonio Conti the work started from the portico next to the shrine and ended in 1721.
5bf676b7-c1ac-53ed-8e80-eafc74f0d3c4.location: Exterior, Santuario della Beata Vergine di san Luca
5bf676b7-c1ac-53ed-8e80-eafc74f0d3c4.artist: Camillo Saccenti; Gian Giacomo Monti; Giovanni Antonio Conti

5d883aff-c791-5728-975f-c3f848744787.name: Upper Synagogue
5d883aff-c791-5728-975f-c3f848744787.description: Form the 15th century onwards, part of the area below the chateau became a cultural and spiritual centre for the Moravian Jewish community. There was a Talmudic school, 12 synagogues and other places of worship. In the second half of the 16th century the legendary Rabbi Löw, allegedly the creator of the Prague golem, worked there. After a fire, the buildings and the synagogue were restored by master builders of the court. The synagogue is the only extant example of a “Polish-style” temple in Czech lands. It features four cupolas supported by four columns standing in the centre of a hall. The adjacent Jewish cemetery is among the largest and oldest in the Czech Republic.

60118261-bf39-5b51-becf-89deec2d3d9c.name: Invention of the Holy Cross
60118261-bf39-5b51-becf-89deec2d3d9c.description: The Counter-Reformation activities of the Capuchin order are reflected in this sizeable picture for the high altar. It depicts a key scene in the legend of the Invention of the Holy Cross on which Christ was crucified, showing Empress Helen, the mother of Constantine the Great, as she witnesses the Cross's authenticity; that the touch of the cross brings a dead youth back to life and cures a terminally-ill woman. Behind the empress stands Bishop Makarios. The use of light within the picture makes much of the resurrection, while the rhetorical gestures, artistic rendering of richly varied surfaces and a monumental compositional structure, make for an impressive painting. The canvas, considered the first Baroque painting in Moravia, originated at the same time as the *Crucifixion* Sandrart painted for the Cathedral of St. Stephen in Vienna, which was said to have been commissioned by Count Václav Eusebius of Lobkowitz, one of the most powerful men in the Viennese imperial court.
60118261-bf39-5b51-becf-89deec2d3d9c.location: Capuchin Monastery and the Church of the Invention of the Holy Cross

6170eca7-efbd-5cb1-8474-f0ef9b1c591c.name: Carillons
6170eca7-efbd-5cb1-8474-f0ef9b1c591c.description: A Flanders-made ensemble of two carillons with 92 bells commissioned by King D. João V, representing the world’s largest historical set. The north tower carillon has 45 bells and the south tower carillon 47 bells. The bells are made of bronze and their total weight is 217 tons. According to tradition, when the king was told the astronomic price of only one carillon, he answered "I didn't expect it to be that cheap, I'll have two."

667bd081-852f-55d6-9cc7-bc832e3888f1.name: Christ Collapsing under the Cross
667bd081-852f-55d6-9cc7-bc832e3888f1.description: Havelka’s artistic expression and exaggeration of shape was rooted in F. A. Maulbertsch’s style, which was possibly mediated by J. Winterhalder Jr. or J. W. Bergl. Havelka developed his style to the full in the dramatic Stations of the Cross cycle. F. A. Sebastini, an associate of Maulbertsch, worked on the decoration of Count Salm’s residence in Sloup at the same time.
667bd081-852f-55d6-9cc7-bc832e3888f1.artist: Josef Ignác Havelka (1716 Ústí nad Orlicí – 1788 Brno)

68654a80-6367-5fad-a886-df3ed8762563.name: Stucco cartouche
68654a80-6367-5fad-a886-df3ed8762563.description: The authorship of the excellent stuccowork has not been recorded although, undoubtedly, the master craftsman was a member of the Wessobrunn school. The attribution to Franz Xaver Feichtmayr, possibly with the involvement of his brother Johann Michael, is considered reliable. It is composed of rocaille stucco of the greatest refinement, which in parts has been executed in free sculptural forms and open work. As they ascend, the broad, bold forms in the lower section of the spandrel become increasingly delicate, and against the background of the main fresco dissolve into fragile vegetative tendrils, whose free play of forms also disrupts the symmetry of the cartouche. The rear-view figure in the spandrel fresco is reputedly a self-portrait of Matthäus Günther.
68654a80-6367-5fad-a886-df3ed8762563.location: West nave bay, southeast vault spandrel
68654a80-6367-5fad-a886-df3ed8762563.artist: Franz Xaver Feichtmayr the elder (1698–1763, attributed) and his brother Johann Michael Feichtmayr (1696–1772, attributed)

6b1e3b8c-0d8c-5527-b9d3-642e4b7b458f.name: Bethlehem Chapel
6b1e3b8c-0d8c-5527-b9d3-642e4b7b458f.description: The Burial Chapel of the Virgin Mary is followed by a two-storey building loosely designed after Christ’s tomb in Jerusalem. On the ground floor are marble reliefs of the Birth of Christ, the Adoration of the Magi and the Flight into Egypt; on the first floor there is a chapel featuring Mary Magdalene and the corpse of Christ.
6b1e3b8c-0d8c-5527-b9d3-642e4b7b458f.location: Pilgrimage Church of the Elevation of the Holy Cross, Jaroměřice u Jevíčka

6c2db2b6-bf95-5968-8435-b88d7d3acfd9.name: High Altar
6c2db2b6-bf95-5968-8435-b88d7d3acfd9.location: Sanctuary, Votive church of St. Mary of Jerusalem, Trški Vrh, near Krapina

6c85a65f-6ff4-5d91-8ae5-f984c4d54097.name: Chapel of St. Joseph
6c85a65f-6ff4-5d91-8ae5-f984c4d54097.description: The altarpiece represents St. Joseph, husband to the Mother of the Lord. The artist, who trained in Swabia, settled in Vienna after a journey to Italy and supplied altarpieces for Moravian churches. The tabernacle and reliquaries were originally part of the high altar. The glass case (1750) contains a wax figurine with relics of St. Liberata, donated by Pope Benedict XIV.

6f0f07b0-eee8-503e-a5b8-02651b202a00.name: General view of the Stairway of the Five Senses and the Fountain of Vision  and of  Taste
6f0f07b0-eee8-503e-a5b8-02651b202a00.description: This stairway continues the theme of the hierarchy of the five senses, as if revealing in the ascending course the degree of corporeity that should be attributed to each of the senses. The mythological figures found at the axis of the fountain were re-“Christianised” by order of the Censorial Court in 1774 having previously been considered “indecorous” due to their proximity to the biblical figures. The figures – whose original denominations are well known – were maintained and only the inscriptions were changed.
6f0f07b0-eee8-503e-a5b8-02651b202a00.location: The Stairway of the Five Senses, Bom Jesus de Braga Sanctuary (Bom Jesus do Monte)

74d429db-0e98-5a57-908f-8cf2399a89f7.name: Loreto and the so-called Náchod Chapel (St Anna church)
74d429db-0e98-5a57-908f-8cf2399a89f7.description: The Cardinal had a pilgrimage chapel built within the Capuchin Monastery in 1622. The chapel, modelled on an Italian Loreto to symbolise the Holy stable, the birthplace of Christ, was the first of its kind in Czech lands. In 1636 the Church of St. Anne was constructed next to the chapel, with a statue of the Black Madonna the scourge of the heretics. The complex was richly decorated with statues and stuccos. The church and the Loreto were destroyed by fire; only the chancel and the Náchod Chapel survive.

75199fa6-69bb-5d9b-b18f-1369a12f7cc8.name: The Holy Trinity
75199fa6-69bb-5d9b-b18f-1369a12f7cc8.description: The topmost sculpture of Christ the Saviour and God the Father, the ruler of the world, opens with the Archangel Michael, symbol of the eternal struggle against heresy. The dove of the Holy Spirit on a sunburst has its eminence underlined by the rays of the rising sun. Even the Augsburg masters took an interest in the gilding of the copper statues.
75199fa6-69bb-5d9b-b18f-1369a12f7cc8.artist: Ondřej Zahner (1709 Ettershausen – 1752 Olomouc), Jan Šimon Forstner (1714? Salzburg – 1773 Olomouc)

759ac58d-d5a3-5acd-ba7a-9d489af7bf33.name: Vaulting
759ac58d-d5a3-5acd-ba7a-9d489af7bf33.description: The symbol of St. John of Nepomuk at the top of the vaulting is the central motif of the church interior. It is a symbol repeated in the shape of the pointed windows; their incorporation into “lantern” chapels above the entrance vestibules, resembles a sword in a sheath. The metaphor also appears in the legend of St. John of Nepomuk; he refused to break the confidentiality of the confessional, his tongue being like a sword in a sheath.
759ac58d-d5a3-5acd-ba7a-9d489af7bf33.location: Interior, Church of St. John of Nepomuk

76936470-37f5-5740-97e3-6a78439dffef.name: Abbot’s Coronation Sceptre
76936470-37f5-5740-97e3-6a78439dffef.description: The spiral part of the sceptre is covered with acanthus leaves and multi-coloured cut glass. In the central halo there is an image of the Madonna of Old Brno transferred into relief form as a cast statue.

7701e3b1-be74-5694-b46e-d3d7094df40f.name: Main Chapel, interior
7701e3b1-be74-5694-b46e-d3d7094df40f.description: Main altarpiece with a huge retable decorated in *azulejos* in the so called National style. In the centre of the retable there is a reliquary in gilt silver donated by the pilgrims of Lisbon in 1680, it holds the image of Our Lady of Cape Espichel.
7701e3b1-be74-5694-b46e-d3d7094df40f.location: Sanctuary of Our Lady of Cape Espichel

77da7614-9b91-52f9-a8f6-51683004bb06.name: Panelled ceiling
77da7614-9b91-52f9-a8f6-51683004bb06.description: Presumably the work of master craftsmen schooled in secular architecture, the nave features a wooden panelled ceiling composed of rectangular and octagonal panels and gilded rosettes. Due to the intricacy and interlacing of the panels it was never intended for a programme of pictures. Nevertheless, it lends the space the character of a festive hall and heightens the impression generated by the altars.

7bdc50c1-c5b6-5f3d-a9fb-5eab3d2363fe.name: *Mark the Evangelist*
7bdc50c1-c5b6-5f3d-a9fb-5eab3d2363fe.location: Pulpit, Parish Church of Our Lady of the Snow

7d79aec6-af13-5110-a27e-45a7ec8a4d19.name: Fountain of the Five Holy Wounds
7d79aec6-af13-5110-a27e-45a7ec8a4d19.description: The motto for the theme of the senses is given by the first fountain, which refers precisely to the Suffering of Christ, and presents the symbolism that summarises the *Via Crucis*: The Five Holy Wounds Fountain. The fountain tablet presents in relief the instruments of the Passion of Christ.
7d79aec6-af13-5110-a27e-45a7ec8a4d19.location: The Stairway of the Five Senses, Bom Jesus de Braga Sanctuary (Bom Jesus do Monte)

8040d180-a30b-5c06-b882-58cee878370d.name: *St. Stephen* (Altar of St. Stephen)
8040d180-a30b-5c06-b882-58cee878370d.description: The young deacon, Stephen, is shown in a scene of apotheosis, surrounded by a wreath of clouds and a halo.
8040d180-a30b-5c06-b882-58cee878370d.location: Central inter-columnation of the Altar of St Stephen (south chapel), Parish Church of Our Lady of the Snow
8040d180-a30b-5c06-b882-58cee878370d.artist: Circle of the sculptor, Filip (Philipp) Jakob Straub (1706–1774)

80a1b956-25ac-5fbb-95b6-df261b896bca.name: Church of the Name of the Virgin Mary with residence of the Premonstratensian order
80a1b956-25ac-5fbb-95b6-df261b896bca.description: The model shows the ideal appearance of the church and residence that were not completed. Santini’s original design did not include a tower in the frontage, while the shape of the church held more true to the Marian star, as in other of the architect’s designs. The complex came into existence through the construction of the new church and its link with the Chapel of St. Anne; the chapel opposite was to be dedicated to St. Joseph.

811c78b3-34d9-54df-bc61-6623d14d26f2.name: Pulpit
811c78b3-34d9-54df-bc61-6623d14d26f2.description: The pulpit from the sculptor Moll from Innsbruck is an especially opulent example of a Baroque pulpit. The richly curved forms of the foot, parapet and baldachin feature a wealth of figures and symbols, including personifications of the divine virtues at the foot of the cupola and evangelist symbols on the baldachin.

8128a2ad-ec2b-5fac-8598-45527014f650.name: View to the Sanctuary
8128a2ad-ec2b-5fac-8598-45527014f650.location: Votive church of St. Mary of Jerusalem, Trški Vrh, near Krapina
8128a2ad-ec2b-5fac-8598-45527014f650.artist: Architect: Josef Hoffer (1700–1764); builder: Josip Javornik (active c. 1750); painter: Anton Joseph (Jožef) Lerchinger (Lerhinger) (c. 1720–after 1787)

83bec619-3cc0-5537-81cf-5de75419f325.name: *Azulejos* depicting the legend of the Miraculous Finding of the Image of Our Lady
83bec619-3cc0-5537-81cf-5de75419f325.description: These 18th-century panels recall the legend of the Miraculous Finding of the Image of Our Lady at the site.
83bec619-3cc0-5537-81cf-5de75419f325.location: Memory Hermitage, interior, Sanctuary of Our Lady of Cape Espichel

83c8fa85-4413-5d4d-90af-066b8e8a993e.name: The Stigmatisation of St. Francis
83c8fa85-4413-5d4d-90af-066b8e8a993e.description: Rotter, who specialised in altarpieces, easel paintings, frescos and decorative wall paintings, was a major figure within the Brno guild of painters. His oeuvre is known from the 1740s, when he worked for the Augustinians and Premonstratensians in Hradisko near Olomouc, although the frescos are not preserved. The side-altar picture comes from Rotter’s late phase, when he embraced closed shapes and more simple colour schemes.
83c8fa85-4413-5d4d-90af-066b8e8a993e.location: Capuchin Monastery and the Church of the Invention of the Holy Cross, Brno

83d3decd-9c3a-5aca-8af7-4d9325db876f.name: Right hand-side altar
83d3decd-9c3a-5aca-8af7-4d9325db876f.description: The artistic highlight of the ensemble is the right hand-side altar from unpainted Swiss pine wood, probably the work of the carver Michael Lechleitner from Grins. The altar, which according to the inscription was donated by Susanne Kolp and Elisabeth Linser in 1652, is one of the most important German Early Baroque altars. In continuation of Late Gothic traditions it is covered in rich ornamental carvings from the repertoire of the Late Renaissance, while the overall form – a column aedicule raised on a high plinth with a vertical oval altar crown – is already characterised by Baroque forms.
83d3decd-9c3a-5aca-8af7-4d9325db876f.location: Southeast nave on the triumphal arch wall

84897501-b74e-51a6-8afc-b37c98e434cb.name: Sketch of the frontage
84897501-b74e-51a6-8afc-b37c98e434cb.description:
The building, designed by Santini, was executed by local master bricklayers.  
The sketch shows that a double staircase in the front leading to the gallery opposite the high altar was dropped. The basic layout and volume of the building were thus geometrised into perfect symmetry – situated on top of a hill – between heaven and earth.

87188e70-5901-5074-a091-18da8ed50017.name: High altar
87188e70-5901-5074-a091-18da8ed50017.description: The Baroque modification of the church was preceded by the exhumation of the remains of St. Notburga. The bones, in the form of a whole-body relic with rich garments housed in a glass shrine, were integrated into the altar in 1740. The bulky, two-storey altar with free-standing columns and a baldachin in the altar crown served as a form of triumphal gate between earth and heaven with the saint as mediator. Two of the outer saintly figures, Leopold and Emperor Heinrich II are attributed to Franz Xaver Nißl.

873474e2-e2a6-57ee-9fc2-5d408be01607.name: Angel
873474e2-e2a6-57ee-9fc2-5d408be01607.description: Monumental statues of angels on the perimeter ledge bear symbols of the Virgin Mary invocated by the Litany of the Virgin Mary.
873474e2-e2a6-57ee-9fc2-5d408be01607.artist: Anton Schweigl (1700 Gaiming in Tirol – 1761 Brno)

8817f196-3685-51fa-b249-38607df00ba9.name: Northern side façade
8817f196-3685-51fa-b249-38607df00ba9.description: Religious motifs are no longer to be found on the side façades instead they are completely devoted to the amusement of the viewer. While the south side features a false window with a woman looking out, the north side is largely decorated with exotic animals in accordance with the fashion of the time. Three monkeys are sitting on the cornice with a basket of fruit, above them a parrot on a stick and a cat at the other end of the cornice.

88c7204a-23d1-51ef-a375-c6869cf50789.name: General view
88c7204a-23d1-51ef-a375-c6869cf50789.description: The rich iconographic decorative program of the oratory celebrates the Trinity with stories from the Old and New Testament.
88c7204a-23d1-51ef-a375-c6869cf50789.artist: Lionello Spada, Francesco Brizio and Lucio Massari

8aaa5906-7f55-546c-b7da-d0174d9c8d33.name: Painted ceiling (central medallion)
8aaa5906-7f55-546c-b7da-d0174d9c8d33.description: A type of ceiling painting known as *di sotto* *in sù* (“above from below”), designed to create the illusion that the figures are suspended above the viewer when seen from below. The Ascension of the Virgin is influenced by Rubens' *di sotto* *in su* ceilings. The Triumph of the Mother of God oval medallion is contained within *ferronneries*.

8ac4cf22-50d5-5b6f-aa87-7f91455fb3ac.name: Water House
8ac4cf22-50d5-5b6f-aa87-7f91455fb3ac.description: Hexagonally shaped, the interior of the water house has running benches and is decorated with *azulejos*, the narrative of which involves scenes of leisure and pilgrimage (today completely destroyed). At the far end, there is a small house-shaped fountain decorated in smooth relief and with a protruding key. It is surmounted by a triangular pediment with a valve in the fauces of a stone lion.
8ac4cf22-50d5-5b6f-aa87-7f91455fb3ac.location: Sanctuary of Our Lady of Cape Espichel, East end

8aeeb74e-0d4f-5071-922e-9d1cbcceeefc.name: View to the Choir
8aeeb74e-0d4f-5071-922e-9d1cbcceeefc.location: Votive church of St. Mary of Jerusalem, Trški Vrh, near Krapina
8aeeb74e-0d4f-5071-922e-9d1cbcceeefc.artist: Architect: Josef Hoffer (1700–1764); builder: Josip Javornik (active c. 1750); painter: Anton Joseph (Jožef) Lerchinger (Lerhinger) (c. 1720–after 1787)

8b35ea4f-b3dc-5188-83e9-65b089384de4.name: Chancel
8b35ea4f-b3dc-5188-83e9-65b089384de4.description: The chancel is completely covered with gilded and carved woodwork. In the centre of the altar stands the miraculous image of Our Lord of Matosinhos flanked by Late Renaissance stone figures.
8b35ea4f-b3dc-5188-83e9-65b089384de4.location: Interior, Sanctuary of Bom Jesus de Matosinhos
8b35ea4f-b3dc-5188-83e9-65b089384de4.artist: Portuguese woodcarvers: Luís Pereira da Costa (active 1724–?), Domingos Martins Moreira (active 1746–1750)

8b8d95b0-01c3-5050-9691-e08552b65528.name: Scourged Christ
8b8d95b0-01c3-5050-9691-e08552b65528.description: The miraculous statue was brought by a monk to Louka Monastery from the Steingaden Monastery in Bavaria. It is a replica of an Adoration statue in the local *Wieskirche*. The statue was first placed on a side altar in the old Church of St. Lawrence where it was believed to heal the sick and enjoyed enormous respect. When a new church was built on the site the statue was installed at the high altar. The church decoration was determined by the new dedication to the Scourged Christ.
8b8d95b0-01c3-5050-9691-e08552b65528.location: Pilgrimage Church of the Scourged Saviour, Dyje

8d3b4ed2-289b-509f-9057-e51b50094952.name: Celebration of the Virgin Mary
8d3b4ed2-289b-509f-9057-e51b50094952.description: The ceiling painting blends in with the architecture illustrating apocrypha from the Book of Sirach. The painting is a metaphorical celebration of the Virgin Mary as the embodiment of Divine Wisdom: angels with mirrors serve to enlighten visitors.

8ef6164d-8b25-56fd-9a75-9a922be66c14.name: Mass Chalice and Jugs
8ef6164d-8b25-56fd-9a75-9a922be66c14.description: Apart from the chalice decorated with half-figures of the order’s saints painted on enamel, and jugs for Abbot Zirckl, there were two other chalices for assisting priests, with scenes from the Lfe and Torment of St. John of Nepomuk and the Passion, created in the Augsburg workshop for the coronation.

9457f0e4-3fcf-50a6-aec1-b755319d7119.name: Ground-plan reconstruction
9457f0e4-3fcf-50a6-aec1-b755319d7119.description: The original ground plan was altered by the construction of the sacristy and oratory. The symbolic design of a four-apse central construction is an allusion on the “double” temple in Jerusalem, close to the Holy Grave.
9457f0e4-3fcf-50a6-aec1-b755319d7119.artist: František Benedikt Klíčník? (1677 Ivanovice na Hané – 1755 Brno)

97b7bc59-bda4-53ec-9bcc-8d85ce39a695.name: The Saint
97b7bc59-bda4-53ec-9bcc-8d85ce39a695.description: The sculpted decoration of the church was created by a leading Brno sculptor Ondřej Schweigl, a graduate of the Vienna Academy. The surface finish is by the master gilder V. Kutálek, the artist’s son-in-law, and with whom he collaborated in, for example, nearby Křtiny.
97b7bc59-bda4-53ec-9bcc-8d85ce39a695.location: Pilgrimage Church of the Virgin Mary of Dolours

9893bb4f-5bee-56e3-82dc-7febef951947.name: Immaculate Conception
9893bb4f-5bee-56e3-82dc-7febef951947.description: In 1646, on restoration of Portugal’s Independence from Spain, King João IV officially consecrated Portugal to the Virgin of the Immaculate Conception. Depictions of scenes from the Life of the Virgin go back to the earliest days of Christian art but it is unusual to see this particular scene depicted.

9927d984-2b47-57ca-b768-827d5abf75c0.name: High altar and miraculous picture
9927d984-2b47-57ca-b768-827d5abf75c0.description: The high altar is one of the most important examples of the Baroque staging of an older sacred picture. The miraculous picture *Mariahilf* from Lucas Cranach was originally housed in Dresden and found its way to Innsbruck as a gift to Archduke Leopold V. It has been on display in the parish church since 1650. It became the most widespread picture of the Virgin Mary in the alpine region. It was integrated into the high altar, built in 1726, as a “picture within a picture” (with exchangeable frames, which during Lent displays a picture from Josef Schöpf, at all other times a silver frame). The high altar is flanked by statues of the patron saints of the Diocese of Brixen, Ingenuin and Albuin.
9927d984-2b47-57ca-b768-827d5abf75c0.artist: Lucas Cranach the Elder (1472–1553); Cristoforo Benedetti (1660–1735), Theodor Benedetti [n.d.]; Josef Schöpf (1745–1822)

9e2fc162-268d-5843-8639-395c51330ad4.name: Flower decoration
9e2fc162-268d-5843-8639-395c51330ad4.description: The festive atmosphere of the interior is enhanced by the rich decoration and flower ornamentation of the quadraturist, Greiner, and the still-life painter, Zagelmann.
9e2fc162-268d-5843-8639-395c51330ad4.location: Pilgrimage Church of the Virgin Mary of Dolours, Detail of the Fresco
9e2fc162-268d-5843-8639-395c51330ad4.artist: Johann Zagelmann (1720 Těšín – 1758 Vienna), Anton Greiner

a0121cc0-20a3-5469-8da2-4993a1e95a3a.name: Main façade
a0121cc0-20a3-5469-8da2-4993a1e95a3a.description: The end side facing the Untermarkt is the magnificently decorated main façade of the house with a central bay window. Architecture paintings form the structure and frame for the images. At the bay window the central motifs are presented, in the middle below the window the Mary Help picture from Innsbruck carried by putti, above it God the Father and the Holy Ghost. On the side walls further putti are depicted playing with a wind wheel and bird cage, while the putti to the side of the bay window present the Tablets of the Law with the Ten Commandments, the Cross of Christ and a chalice. The gable zone features a peacock. The overall appearance is primarily a result of the virtuoso rocaille frames around the windows. Cornice and gable, both painted, form the upper termination.

a087cbc7-2a72-565a-9130-17dbf4bd2cf2.name: Side chapel, right (Our Lord of Passos Chapel and Our Lady of Soledad)
a087cbc7-2a72-565a-9130-17dbf4bd2cf2.location: Interior, Sanctuary of Bom Jesus de Matosinhos
a087cbc7-2a72-565a-9130-17dbf4bd2cf2.artist: Portuguese woodcarvers: Luís Pereira da Costa (active 1724–?), Domingos Martins Moreira (active 1746–1750)

a2714513-34b3-581b-8817-44074b61fd72.name: Frescos on the ceiling of the cupola
a2714513-34b3-581b-8817-44074b61fd72.description: The frescoes on the crossing cupola form an organisational system which simultaneously blends with and transcends the architecture. Free-standing columns appear to support a type of dome which encloses the base of the skylight turret. Between the columns a central scene from the Legend of the Cross is depicted in each of the four axial directions respectively: the “bronze serpent”, as well as the discovery, raising and veneration of the cross by the martyrs.
a2714513-34b3-581b-8817-44074b61fd72.location: Crossing cupola, Catholic Pilgrimage Church of the Holy Cross

a72619dd-8151-59b9-940a-aea86096b247.name: Altar of St. John of Nepomuk
a72619dd-8151-59b9-940a-aea86096b247.description: The essential features of the sculptures are in the independently decorative luxuriance of the drapery, which in places grows into abstractly dramatic labyrinths, hiding in its mass the body of the saints; a plastic mass of clothing that with its abundance of folds and deep shadow hides its volume. The expressive faces, with deep, emphatic lines on the noses and eyelids, correlate well with this overall modelling.
a72619dd-8151-59b9-940a-aea86096b247.location: Right-hand side altar in the main nave, Franciscan Church and Monastery of Our Lady of Trsat

a7d38155-17fa-5bba-9425-30187706f79f.name: Cupola
a7d38155-17fa-5bba-9425-30187706f79f.description: The pillars continue in four pendentives with allegories of Europe, Asia, Africa and America (J. K. Handke, 1731); the niches feature statues of the Evangelists. The stucco decoration divides the vaulting into six cartouches, the frescos of which represent Old Testament accounts of Sara, Rebecca, Abigail, Bathsheba, Judith and Ester – prototypes of the Virgin Mary. The upper third of the cartouches contain invocations of the prayer *Salve Regina* (Steger, 1677). The cupola, centralising the longitudinal building, is crowned with a lantern and a dove, symbol of the Holy Spirit.
a7d38155-17fa-5bba-9425-30187706f79f.artist: Baldassare Fontana (1661–1733, Chiasso), Jan Kryštof Handke (1694 Janovice u Rýmařova – 1774 Olomouc)

aa5845ce-589a-5523-b9b6-1dd7e994fc46.name: The Altar of St. Peter and Paul (High altar)
aa5845ce-589a-5523-b9b6-1dd7e994fc46.description: The magnificent high altar, put up with red Veronese marble, fills out the central axis of the chancel and is flanked by large windows. A series of elegant columns dramatically envelope the mensa and retable. As emissaries of the Heavenly Hosts, angels with harps stand beside the attic storey which inside bears a halo of light (so-called gloriole) representing God. They look upon Günther’s altarpiece, which displays the glory of the church’s patrons. Flanking the columns  four statues represent other saints who are important to the parish.
aa5845ce-589a-5523-b9b6-1dd7e994fc46.artist: Designer unknown; altar painting: Matthäus Günther (1705–88)

ac0222e4-7fae-5d3e-bc11-b8b5d0857467.name: High Altar
ac0222e4-7fae-5d3e-bc11-b8b5d0857467.description: Two sculptures from the Pacassi workshop: *St. Francis* on the left and *St. John the Evangelist* on the right.
ac0222e4-7fae-5d3e-bc11-b8b5d0857467.location: Presbytery, Franciscan Church and Monastery of Our Lady of Trsat

af670ccd-204f-5459-abf8-9e8b73bfa098.name: High Altar
af670ccd-204f-5459-abf8-9e8b73bfa098.description: Built thanks to the generosity of Viceroy Baltazar Bedeković and his wife, Helena Rozalija Somogy, the main altar's massive construction meets the full width and height of the sanctuary. According to the inscription on the cartouche at the top of the retable the altar was completed in 1743, although the sculpture of *Immaculate Mary* at the centre belonged to the old dismantled main altar made in 1729.
af670ccd-204f-5459-abf8-9e8b73bfa098.location: Presbytery, Parish Church of Our Lady of the Snow
af670ccd-204f-5459-abf8-9e8b73bfa098.artist: Circle of the sculptor  Filip (Philipp) Jakob Straub (1706–1774)

afd811b1-ad49-5351-8f64-cc37ff31078e.name: *Our Lady of the Snow hovering over the Church of Kutina and inhabitants of the city*
afd811b1-ad49-5351-8f64-cc37ff31078e.description: In the *trompe l'œil* *rocaille* framework there is a representation of Vicar Antun Pozojević and Count Karlo II Erdödy with the newly erected church of Kutina, surrounded by its covered walkway. The Immaculate Virgin Mary with a scapular on her arm hovers above them.
afd811b1-ad49-5351-8f64-cc37ff31078e.location: Sanctuary ceiling, Parish Church of Our Lady of the Snow

b2980c5d-4b8e-5737-b1bd-ebbf38274aad.name: High altar
b2980c5d-4b8e-5737-b1bd-ebbf38274aad.description: The high altar, which according to an inscription on the predella was built in 1651 as an endowment of the Weinzierl family, is the oldest of the three altars in the Church. It is an aedicula altar with a broken segmental pediment and an openwork altar crown. At the centre of the programme of figures are the church’s three patron saints, all of whom are invoked as protection from the plague.

b3dc84c7-1930-5b07-b085-55d198c770fa.name: St. Vincent and St. Sebastian
b3dc84c7-1930-5b07-b085-55d198c770fa.description: Depicting the Martyrs St. Sebastian and St. Vincent, these sculptures represent just two pieces from The Royal Commission, which includes among other precious items 56 Italian sculptures, representing the most important collection of Italian Baroque sculpture outside Italy. The two sculptures illustrated here are made from marble; each one is 3.58-meters tall.

b478afb3-6caa-520b-bcbb-1a527eca0896.name: St. John the Baptist
b478afb3-6caa-520b-bcbb-1a527eca0896.description: The individual, larger-than-life figures are veiled in light, airy cloaks. Their austere gesticulation and postures correspond with their spiritual facial expressions. The picturesque outlines of the figures enhance the aesthetic impression of a pyramid-like whole. Following Zahner’s death the sculptural decoration was completed by W. Träger and J. M. Scherhauf. They continued with the sculptor’s initial concept and achieved features typical of Zahner in a side-altar figure for the Místek Church.

b4d6753b-ee3a-5120-a57e-e35af32589c1.name: Hall of the Ancestors
b4d6753b-ee3a-5120-a57e-e35af32589c1.description: The monumental and technically demanding building on an unusual elliptical ground plan, celebrates a Swabian-Bavarian dynasty that settled in Moravia in the second half of the 16th century. Statues in the niches represent real and mythical family figures. Erlach followed in the footsteps of Bernini in the design. The memorial building changed function in the mid-18th century when the Hall, with its pre-Romanticism terraces, became a viewing point for surveying the beautiful countryside around the chateau.
b4d6753b-ee3a-5120-a57e-e35af32589c1.artist: Johann Bernhard Fischer von Erlach (1656 Graz – 1723 Vienna), Tobias Kracker (1658–1736, Vienna)

bb4dd8ab-cc0e-5fac-aef4-60091ca7be8d.name: The Four Latin Church Fathers
bb4dd8ab-cc0e-5fac-aef4-60091ca7be8d.description: The statues of the Four Latin Church Fathers, still animated with restrained Baroque pathos, rank as the best works of their creator.
bb4dd8ab-cc0e-5fac-aef4-60091ca7be8d.location: Column pairs in the lay church on the sides of the transept

be3b668a-5d87-5793-9bef-a8d5f0482e41.name: Panoramic view of the church interior
be3b668a-5d87-5793-9bef-a8d5f0482e41.description: Commissioned by the wealthy merchant, Manuel Álvares Azeitado, this is the first *scarto* known in Portugal, forming part of the International Baroque program. The panoramic view of the interior shows the *trompe l'œil* architecture of the barrel-vaulted ceiling, which appears to be a continuation of the walls. The *trompe l'œil,* centred towards one focal point, creates the illusion of deep recession, heavenly sphere or even an open sky.
be3b668a-5d87-5793-9bef-a8d5f0482e41.artist: Woodcarvers: João de Touro Freitas, António de Oliveira (1675–n.d.), Manuel João da Fonseca and Francisco da Silva (1684-n.d.); painters: António de Oliveira Bernardes (1662–1732) and Pedro Figueira; azulejos painters: Gabriel del Barco (1649–c.1703)

c2fa115e-3ff1-53bd-a4fb-c6aa6c675900.name: Examples of *Via Crucis* chapels: Chapel of the Flagellation and the Mercury Fountain; Chapel of the Crucifixion and the interior of the Chapel of the Falls
c2fa115e-3ff1-53bd-a4fb-c6aa6c675900.description: The Stairway of the Five Senses leads up to the Crucifixion Chapel. On the way up are other chapels one of which, the Chapel of the Flagellation, reinforces the Suffering of Christ or the *Via Crucis* as an element of purification.
c2fa115e-3ff1-53bd-a4fb-c6aa6c675900.location: The Stairway of the Five Senses, Bom Jesus de Braga (Bom Jesus do Monte)

c6225da7-41a1-5706-82f3-6f3e9e2d0c24.name: Façade
c6225da7-41a1-5706-82f3-6f3e9e2d0c24.description: The façade, originally planned with bolder mouldings and greater richness, is only distantly related to that of the Innsbruck parish church (since 1964 St. Jacob’s Cathedral). The architectural idea in Wilten is a different one: While at St. Jacob’s the central section between the towers is set back, here a lightly rounded, projecting broken pediment sets column-like accents. These form the framework for the central section with its shallow concave form. United under a tail gable the central section forms the main motif, while in contrast, at the Innsbruck parish church the central section was clearly subordinated to the pair of towers. The statue of the Mary Immaculata and the portal are the work of Joseph Stapf.
c6225da7-41a1-5706-82f3-6f3e9e2d0c24.artist: Franz de Paula Penz (1702–1772), Joseph Stapf [n.d.]

c6cb3e56-81b8-5635-ab45-fa274e89c1c4.name: Ceiling fresco
c6cb3e56-81b8-5635-ab45-fa274e89c1c4.description: Following his apprenticeship, Schöpf, a student of Knoller, is considered one of the most important masters of fresco painting during the transition to Early Classicism. The composition of the large cupola fresco depicting the Coronation of the Virgin Mary follows the Late Baroque scheme with a crown of clouds and vision of light in the centre, however the painting style, above all in the case of the figures, is characterised by concentration and devout earnestness. Baroque pathos is replaced by a salutary pictorial narrative.

c6e385c3-ce5d-59a2-9749-9c9b67369cb0.name: St. Cyril
c6e385c3-ce5d-59a2-9749-9c9b67369cb0.description: The six statues on the central section represent Slavic saints: Methodius, the first Moravian bishop; Cyril (Konstantin); Vojtěch the Bishop of Prague and founder of the first Benedictine Monastery in Bohemia; John of Nepomuk; John Sarkander, tortured to death in Olomouc in 1620; and St. Blasius to whom the Olomouc Church, considered the oldest Baroque church in the country, was dedicated.

c808701e-fb13-501f-b5ef-7e36dad27a4e.name: Pulpit
c808701e-fb13-501f-b5ef-7e36dad27a4e.description: A creative reinterpretation of the pulpit by J. B. Straub of 10 years earlier, it stands out in the pantheon of Baroque sculpture in northern Croatia at a time when sculpture and imaginatively and skilfully executed ornamental work were on the threshold of the Rococo.
c808701e-fb13-501f-b5ef-7e36dad27a4e.location: North side of the nave, Parish Church of Our Lady of the Snow

c84f6b86-bda2-5650-b91c-dba0814eb447.name: Remedy Fountain
c84f6b86-bda2-5650-b91c-dba0814eb447.description: Situated in the centre of the Courtyard of the Kings, overlooking the staircase, is an obelisk fountain known as the Remedy Fountain. The obelisk in the centre of the fountain is 14 metres high.
c84f6b86-bda2-5650-b91c-dba0814eb447.location: Courtyard of the Kings, Sanctuary of Our Lady of Good Remedy

c9e437ac-0abc-54f8-bdb1-c612628c79a0.name: Celebration of the Althann Dynasty
c9e437ac-0abc-54f8-bdb1-c612628c79a0.description: Illusionary elements of a balustrade and carpet provide a link between the earth and the celestial sphere. Ancient gods and allegorical figures show a path to honour and glory. The family’s celestial triumph is accompanied by scenes depicting aristocratic virtues. The major component is not stuccowork but painting, in contrast to more recent decorations. The fresco as one of the first pieces by an artist who later became famous.

ca4be14d-93e9-596d-b076-3472190bbd99.name: Left hand-side altar
ca4be14d-93e9-596d-b076-3472190bbd99.description: The left hand-side altar built after 1682 differs fundamentally from the other altars. Its superstructure forms a frame for the two inset paintings; the larger of the two, the actual altarpiece, is the work of Michael Waldmann from 1677 and depicts St. Anthony in front of the Infant Jesus with the portrait of the picture’s donor, the musician Karl Boussier from Innsbruck. The picture was brought to Landeck in 1682. Each side of the altar’s outer frame forms seven small niches with figures of the fourteen Holy Helpers, probably the work of Adam Payr.
ca4be14d-93e9-596d-b076-3472190bbd99.location: Northeast nave on the triumphal arch wall
ca4be14d-93e9-596d-b076-3472190bbd99.artist: Adam Payr (?–1682); Michael Waldmann the younger (1640–1682)

cb50ee45-d844-5c38-ae52-e6a8120cbd02.name: “Black Chapel”
cb50ee45-d844-5c38-ae52-e6a8120cbd02.description: F. A. Rottal had a memorial chapel with a family tomb added to the parish church. Life-size portraits of the investor and his wife adorn the side altars, presenting them as art-loving and pious aristocrats. Together with a relief of Christ on the Mount of Olives, they are considered some of the best work by Gottfried Fritsch, a pupil of G. Donner. At the death of F. A. Rottal, the family died out.

cb712c93-18a3-58c8-9f29-cfea9d8f2763.name: *Mystical Supper of the Holy Family*
cb712c93-18a3-58c8-9f29-cfea9d8f2763.description:
Inscription on the bottom right-hand side:  
*Facta a Fr. Serafino Schön O.M.S. franc. Croatiae Carnioliae An. 1640. Refacta vero a DD. Josepho Candito Italo Neapolitano et Georgio Esperlinn Germano Helveto anno 1777. Mense Augusto.* (Painted by the Franciscan lay brother Seraphin Schön in August 1777; repaired by Italian Joseph (Giuseppe) Candito and German-Swiss Georgio Esperlinn).  
The theme of the painting is the Sacrifice of Christ presented in a tripartite composition in which the central part belongs to the quiet meal of the Holy Family. The food they are eating has a symbolic meaning. On the left, another set table symbolises Christ's Passion carefully arranged by angels and archangels led by St. Michael. On the right-hand side, two large angels are frying fish, while the two small ones are playing with birds, making clear that this painting belongs to the Franciscan Order.
cb712c93-18a3-58c8-9f29-cfea9d8f2763.location: Summer Refectory, west wall, Franciscan Church and Monastery of Our Lady of Trsat

d2a7f2b6-6580-5dae-8336-b155d38a911d.name: Interior, facing east
d2a7f2b6-6580-5dae-8336-b155d38a911d.description: The interior of the Burschlkirche is characterised by the contrast between plane architecture, employing an antiquated repertoire of forms, and the masterfully executed, rich ensemble of the three altars. The two-bay choir with a 3/6 termination in the continuation of the Gothic tradition is separated from the nave by a heavily tapered ogival triumphal arch. This in turn is a simple oblong hall which the panelled ceiling lends the character of a secular festive hall of the Renaissance period.

d2ac0900-9922-5fbf-886a-0210952ff6cd.name: High Altar
d2ac0900-9922-5fbf-886a-0210952ff6cd.description: Perceived as his most monumental work, it is characterised by a light architectural construction that comes out particularly in the concluding, weight-bearing elements where the altar wall is abandoned.
d2ac0900-9922-5fbf-886a-0210952ff6cd.location: Sanctuary, Parish Church of Our Lady of the Snow

d3bb32df-1032-585b-bb84-e5c3b1bb0836.name: *Immaculate Conception*
d3bb32df-1032-585b-bb84-e5c3b1bb0836.location: Ceiling painting in the sanctuary, Votive church of St. Mary of Jerusalem, Trški Vrh, near Krapina

d580e261-d346-5245-927b-14f58847eed8.name: Interior
d580e261-d346-5245-927b-14f58847eed8.description: The overall impression generated by the building’s interior, in fact merely a domed transept square with slanting piers and four barrel-vaulted cross arms, is surprisingly rich. Thanks to the painting, which also includes illusionistic stucco on all the framing, Penz’s clear, well proportioned spatial structure acquires an intricate and appealing character. Architecture and painting thus fuse to form a unity of intricate detail and systematic architectural stringency.
d580e261-d346-5245-927b-14f58847eed8.location: Interior facing south (in the direction of the choir)
d580e261-d346-5245-927b-14f58847eed8.artist: Franz de Paula Penz (1707–1772); Christoph Anton Mayr (c. 1720–1771)

d6131cce-c6f1-5f7e-be6f-984c9b39096b.name: Apotheosis of St. John Sarkander
d6131cce-c6f1-5f7e-be6f-984c9b39096b.description: St. John Sarkander Moravian was a martyr worshipped by the demesne owners, the Kuefstein family. The bridge was a project that would “express their thanks to the Almighty and to celebrate His name always and everywhere”. The picture comes from the side altar in the Chapel of St. Anne, in an infirmary (1743–1745) established as a home for the elderly servants and subjects of the Námešť demesne. A parsonage constructed in parallel was decorated by J. Winterhalder Sr. and K. J. Aigen. The artist P. Troger took part in the decoration of the adjacent church. He was probably introduced to the count – that he had painted a tomb in Röhrenbach for in 1737 – by his friend Winterhalder.
d6131cce-c6f1-5f7e-be6f-984c9b39096b.location: Náměšť nad Oslavou, St. Anne Chapel

d66a89c1-4e7d-50bb-8edb-6b7c02fa1341.name: Pulpit
d66a89c1-4e7d-50bb-8edb-6b7c02fa1341.description: On the corners of the pulpit set on pillars, the figures of the evangelists are shown in high-spirited movement; between them, also plastically very highly emphasised, are *rocaille* cartouches with reliefs in which the central figure is Moses: *Moses Dancing Around the Golden Calf, Moses Receives the Law, Moses and the Bronze Serpent*. Monumentality and dynamism are the main features of the sculptural composition at the top of the baldachin too, showing the *Transfiguration of Christ on Mount Tabor*, the scene enriched with figures of the Prophets *Moses* and *Elijah* either side.
d66a89c1-4e7d-50bb-8edb-6b7c02fa1341.location: North wall of the church, Parish Church of Our Lady of the Snow

d6a6bbee-1004-5fe5-93a3-c845fe7b8380.name: Library
d6a6bbee-1004-5fe5-93a3-c845fe7b8380.description:
A significant Enlightenment Library with around 36,000 volumes amassed through royal commission. It has a cruciform layout with a multi-coloured limestone floor and Rocaille shelves.  
Some rare works furnish its shelves to this day: the *Nuremberg Chronicle* (1493) or the *Theatrvm Orbis Terrarvm* by Ortelius (1595) and a nucleus of scores from musicians such as João de Sousa Carvalho or Marcos Portugal, composed expressly to be played on the Basilica's six organs.

d6d9c08d-bc42-54cc-90c2-ca572c64044c.name: Svatý Kopeček (Holy Hill)
d6d9c08d-bc42-54cc-90c2-ca572c64044c.description: Part of Cardinal Dietrichstein’s Counter-Reformation strategy was the construction of the Church of St. Sebastian on Tanzberg Hill. This pilgrimage church, with 13 chapels of the Stations of the Cross, was intended to turn a rocky hill, redolent with pagan legend, into a “Holy Mount” modelled on Varallo in northern Italy. The original church (G. G. Tencalla) was re-established after 1663 and in 18th and 19th centuries.

d8289a89-1170-5ec0-a741-c5175017f870.name: Chapel of the Holy Trinity
d8289a89-1170-5ec0-a741-c5175017f870.description: This chateau chapel, with a subterranean family tomb, is a conceptual and compositional counterpart to the Hall of the Ancestors. The cylindrical central nave, with six oval apses around the perimeter, is decorated with paintings – the Last Judgment, Heaven and Paradise – drawing attention to the ephemeral nature of existence, the end of human life and its continuation in eternity. The cupola fresco represents the Archangel Michael, the family’s patron saint and protector of the Church.
d8289a89-1170-5ec0-a741-c5175017f870.artist: Johann Bernhard Fischer von Erlach (1656 Graz – 1723 Vienna), Ignaz Heinitz of Heintzenthal (1657–1742, Vienna)

d8c1fd87-1ac6-5fe2-b25b-54927d0e8b27.name: Ecce Homo (“day’s work” or *giornata* of the presbytery fresco)
d8c1fd87-1ac6-5fe2-b25b-54927d0e8b27.description: The Ecce Homo group over the high altar with the statue of the Scourged Christ represents Jesus as the victor over earthly tribulations. The contours outline the “day's work” – *giornata –* showing individual phases of the painting for which fresh plaster had to be applied and into which the artist could paint for up to three days. The sections also show the division of labour between the artist of the illusionary architecture and the painter of the figures.
d8c1fd87-1ac6-5fe2-b25b-54927d0e8b27.location: Pilgrimage Church of the Scourged Saviour, Dyje
d8c1fd87-1ac6-5fe2-b25b-54927d0e8b27.artist: Franz Anton Maulbertsch (1724 Langenargen am Bodensee – 1796 Vienna) and associates

d982fe8c-5b31-5e71-98c1-24e9b98b2b9a.name: Light-bearer
d982fe8c-5b31-5e71-98c1-24e9b98b2b9a.description: Light played a major role in Baroque iconography as a symbol of the Holy Spirit and was synonymous with holiness. Angels, the mediators of God's Will, are represented on the bottom balustrade of the staircase as decorative *putti*, messengers and guardians of the light.
d982fe8c-5b31-5e71-98c1-24e9b98b2b9a.artist: Ondřej Zahner (1709 Ettershausen – 1752 Olomouc) and workshop

dbaffd3f-8c80-55c5-8dff-c3db51a61236.name: Courtyard
dbaffd3f-8c80-55c5-8dff-c3db51a61236.description: Countess Marie Anna Pignatelli took up the reconstruction of the residence after 1722. She commissioned the court architect A. E. Martinelli to build a three-wing chateau, adjust the entrance bridge, parts of the castle front, and the chapel frontage and interior. The two-shouldered staircase of the ceremonial courtyard is set with sculptures of Hercules fighting Antaios and Aeneas Rescuing his Father, Anchises, from Burning Troy.

ddbe9286-c279-56fc-8d46-01cf14d5ad37.name: The Chapel of St. John of Nepomuk
ddbe9286-c279-56fc-8d46-01cf14d5ad37.description: One of the two chapels to the side is dedicated to St. Johann of Nepomuk, the patron saint of the Mittenwald log drivers  on the Isar river. The fresco situated above the chapel’s vault depicts the resurrected martyr, who is crowned by five stars, floating above the Vltava river. A padlock, hanging on the left arm which is gripping a devotional cross, refers to his secrecy.
ddbe9286-c279-56fc-8d46-01cf14d5ad37.location: The southern alcove of the nave

ddf00c3a-e980-51f1-baa7-12826cbb65c4.name: *St. Anne with Saints and the Rovere Family*
