ddf00c3a-e980-51f1-baa7-12826cbb65c4.description: The Virgin Mary with the Infant Jesus and St. Anne in the mid-ground of the composition form the characteristic motif known as "St Anne Selfthird" meaning St Anne with two others (in German, *Die heilige Anna selbdritt*), an iconographic convention that began in the 14th century. On the right-hand side of the composition are members of the Rovere family together with their saint-protectors. On the left-hand side, a Franciscan monk is seen in profile.
ddf00c3a-e980-51f1-baa7-12826cbb65c4.location: Left-hand side altarpiece in St. Anne’s Chapel
ddf00c3a-e980-51f1-baa7-12826cbb65c4.artist: Giovanni Pietro de Pomis (active 1569, Lodi–1633, Graz)

de217671-b0c6-5d52-a68e-4da53f3ccb53.name: Church Façade
de217671-b0c6-5d52-a68e-4da53f3ccb53.description: The late 18th-century Rococo façade is divided into three parts, separated by Corinthian pilasters with capitals, and surmounted by a magnificent pediment built in the 19th century. The two towers, designed in 1848, were completed at the beginning of the 20th century. The pediment dates to around 1890. The first section of the stairway can also be seen in the photograph.
de217671-b0c6-5d52-a68e-4da53f3ccb53.dates: c. 1750; towers: 1848; final design façade: 1880; pediment: c.1890
de217671-b0c6-5d52-a68e-4da53f3ccb53.location: Exterior, Sanctuary of Our Lady of Good Remedy
de217671-b0c6-5d52-a68e-4da53f3ccb53.artist: Church: António Mendes Coutinho (active 1750 ); stairs: Manuel Faustino Loureiro (active1782); Towers: Augusto de Matos Cid (active1880).

de6db7d5-6d7b-5926-ad6b-637eedb72f0d.name: Monochrome roundel with the *Birth of the Virgin*
de6db7d5-6d7b-5926-ad6b-637eedb72f0d.description: The use of monochrome painting in the roundels at the foot of the dome shows Mitelli’s and Colonna’s elegant taste together with their will to emphasise the contrast between the different worlds of the stories of the Virgin and the heavenly vision above. The scene represented in this roundel is strongly indebted to the classicizing style of Guido Reni.
de6db7d5-6d7b-5926-ad6b-637eedb72f0d.location: Dome of the square antechamber of the chapel of the Rosary, Basilica di San Domenico, Bologna
de6db7d5-6d7b-5926-ad6b-637eedb72f0d.artist: Angelo Michele Colonna and Agostino Mitelli

deb66bb9-f9a7-5754-b548-8fe682e92195.name: The Last Judgement
deb66bb9-f9a7-5754-b548-8fe682e92195.description: The brightly coloured main fresco promisingly and obviously thematises the Last Judgement as the goal of Christ’s redemption, whose passion began with His suffering leading up to His crucifixion. Opposite the gate to eternity, before which a toppled Chronos symbolises the end of time, is the throne prepared for Christ as the Judge of the World.

df6b10ce-46a5-5015-8d2f-07ed83b9bdeb.name: Fresco and stucco
df6b10ce-46a5-5015-8d2f-07ed83b9bdeb.description: Perhaps of greatest aesthetic interest is the decorated vault. The fine Wessobrunn stucco with its combination of late-period strapwork and emerging rocailles is the height of the prevailing fashion and is indicative of the transition to Rococo. It probably originates from Franz Xaver Feichtmayr. Thanks to their small format and their general failure to account for viewing from below, the frescos, depicting scenes from the life of the church patroness, appear like inserted folk art pictures. The landscapes depict the environs of Eben. The attribution is contested.
df6b10ce-46a5-5015-8d2f-07ed83b9bdeb.artist: Johann Georg Höttinger (c. 1690–after 1645) or Christoph Anton Mayr (c. 1720–1771); Franz Xaver Feichtmayr (1698–1763)

dfafe781-3027-548f-92da-7716b132333a.name: Invokings and Glories of St. Anthony of Padua
dfafe781-3027-548f-92da-7716b132333a.description: With its capriccio-like tendencies, Holzer’s masterly combination of earthly sceneries and the visionary “celestial realm” follows the concept of illusionistic architecture and marks the peak of the Late Baroque ceiling paintings in Bavaria. The elegance and pathos of the figural depictions are unprecedented. Delicately painted clouds and poetic, brilliant colour shifts account for the enchanting character of the visual experience. As an appeal to the pilgrims, they are encircled by pictorial representations of peoples’ physical and spiritual afflictions: death, fallacy, misery, obsession, plagues, disease, distress at sea, captivity, lameness, material damages and eye conditions; from these ailments the invocation of St. Anthony promises salvation. In this context, there are regional and time-related references, such as: a healed man dragging away his mattress, which is considered to be a self-portrait of the artist; and the merchants that were typical for the social structure of a market town. They are holding a fabric bale and immediately strike the eye when entering the church.

e0b22be9-8f6f-536c-91f7-27d4bf5ef96f.name: *Abraham and the Three Angels*
e0b22be9-8f6f-536c-91f7-27d4bf5ef96f.description: In the third story of the frieze the painter shows the three angels appearing to Abraham to announce the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah as well as his miraculous paternity in old age.

e145a80f-139b-5a44-a72d-22942e7995d1.name: St. Cecilia
e145a80f-139b-5a44-a72d-22942e7995d1.description: This statue of St. Cecilia, an early Christian martyr and patron saint of musicians, was probably created with the intention of commemorating Countess Cecílie Kollonitsch. With her striking attribute (the organ) and female attire, the statue stands out among markedly vertical figures of closed outlines. Her arms stretched forward, and with a cloak thrown over the shoulder, the figure, with the head slightly tilted back, has great emotional appeal.

e3219bac-8d55-51be-9446-ae37aba26277.name: Ceiling paintings *Judith and Holofernes* and *Apocalyptic Madonna*
e3219bac-8d55-51be-9446-ae37aba26277.description: The ceiling frescos in Wilten, which are among the most significant achievements of the Director of the Augsburg Academy, are pictorial worlds executed with virtuosity: heavenly visions open up above grandiose architectural backdrops, which rather than extending the real architecture form part of the visionary event breaking into the space of the church. Like the rhetoric of a Late Baroque preacher, the pictorial content draws a number of references. Here Judith, who presents the head of Holofernes to the people as a symbol of her victory over evil, is interpreted as the precursor of Mary, who at the end of time appears as the “Madonna of the Apocalypse”, the over-comer of all evil. The transcendence of space and time within the picture support this statement.
e3219bac-8d55-51be-9446-ae37aba26277.location: Vault of the west nave bay

e4463aab-b7e7-5517-b782-78afcfe70848.name: *Salvation of the Cross*
e4463aab-b7e7-5517-b782-78afcfe70848.description: The large-scale circumferential main fresco of the church typologically introduces the Holy plan for salvation derived from both the New and Old Testaments. The adjacent choir fresco shows the *Salvation of the Cross* within the illusionistic cupola architecture.
e4463aab-b7e7-5517-b782-78afcfe70848.location: Vault of the nave, side aisles and choir, Catholic Parish and Pilgrimage Church of the Exaltation of the Cross and Our Lady of Sorrows

e4945fc7-7c58-505c-b4ee-a58561295954.name: Church
e4945fc7-7c58-505c-b4ee-a58561295954.description: The church is built in the Late Classical style, the interior following the model of Jesuit churches. Due to the design, the sanctuary is attributed to João Antunes, an attribution that is probable because he was at the time the architect of the Casa do Infantado nearby. The ceiling painting of Our Lady of the Assumption was painted by Lourenço da Cunha in 1740.
e4945fc7-7c58-505c-b4ee-a58561295954.location: Sanctuary of Our Lady of Cape Espichel, West End
e4945fc7-7c58-505c-b4ee-a58561295954.artist: Architecture attributed to João Antunes (1642–1712); painting to Lourenço da Cunha (active 1740–1743)

e4db2e14-2c80-5dda-9994-a2e49390ee72.name: Marienaltar (High Altar)
e4db2e14-2c80-5dda-9994-a2e49390ee72.description: The two-levelled high altar, finished by Feichtmayr, fits into the double-shelled choir apse according to a scenographic plan. The two levels are united through slender column pairs between which the stucco figures of *St. Ulrich* and *St. Norbert* are placed, together with a whimsically cambered attic. All this forms an arcade, which, in turn, frames the slightly removed high altar with its painting of the *Ascension of the Virgin Mary.*
e4db2e14-2c80-5dda-9994-a2e49390ee72.artist: Johann Georg Üblher (1703–1763), Franz Xaver Feichtmayr, the Younger (1735–1803); Franz Georg Hermann, the Younger (1692–1768)

e63e4169-7728-579b-8318-a18d9572838d.name: *St. Kümernissa*
e63e4169-7728-579b-8318-a18d9572838d.description: The bearded St. Kümerrnissa was particularly popular in Tyrol. She was known variously as *Liberatrix, Wilgefortis*, *Ontkomer* and *Hülpe* and can be traced back to the Middle Ages. Her unusual looks relate to the *Volto Santo* from the Tuscan city of Lucca (a wooden cross bearing the corpus of Christ cloaked in the long priest's robe – *colobium*). The development of trade and dissemination of graphic prints representing the famous Tuscan sculpture resulted in an incorrect interpretation of the figure and replacement of the iconography with that of St. Kümerrnissa.

e7e6dced-0a81-539b-82a2-a013d4574cd9.name: Presbytery vaulting
e7e6dced-0a81-539b-82a2-a013d4574cd9.description: The stucco decoration is 30 cm deep in places. The designs for the cartouche frescos were created by M. A. Lublinský, an Olomouc canon and artist. The vault frescos symbolise the invocation of the Loreto litanies. The painting of the Holy Trinity above the altar is accompanied by the Celebration of the Lord by the Three Virtues and the Assumption of the Virgin Mary.
e7e6dced-0a81-539b-82a2-a013d4574cd9.artist: Quiricho Castelli, Domenico Gagina, Carlo Borsa, Matteo Contessa, Martin Antonín Lublinský (1636 Lesnica – 1690 Olomouc).

e8770573-d328-5834-b1d9-a0c8ce5da0f6.name: Bom Jesus Church
e8770573-d328-5834-b1d9-a0c8ce5da0f6.description: At ground level there are two sculptural figures of the prophets, Jeremiah and Isaiah. Over the cornice, on the upper section, are the four evangelists.
e8770573-d328-5834-b1d9-a0c8ce5da0f6.location: Façade of the church in the Neo-Classical style, Bom Jesus de Braga (Bom Jesus do Monte)

eb86b19e-ab63-5c13-b4c8-efb32827e0c8.name: *Choirs of angels with a double crown of flowers and stars*
eb86b19e-ab63-5c13-b4c8-efb32827e0c8.description: Above the extraordinary altar containing the statue of the Virgin Mitelli, and Colonna painted a monumental baroque building, with courts, balconies, friezes and floral decorations. The sky opens over two choirs of angels holding a crown made of flowers, symbolizing earthly grace, and a crown made of stars, a symbol of divine glory. The skilled use of perspective, the vivid colours and the employ of gold leaf in the decorations lead to a strongly visual result.
eb86b19e-ab63-5c13-b4c8-efb32827e0c8.location: Semi dome of the chapel of the Rosary, Basilica di San Domenico, Bologna
eb86b19e-ab63-5c13-b4c8-efb32827e0c8.artist: Angelo Michele Colonna and Agostino Mitelli

ee906e22-472a-58c7-bafa-8ad9e8d52d69.name: Interior of the church
ee906e22-472a-58c7-bafa-8ad9e8d52d69.description: What really defines the internal space is the adoption of half and free standing columns conveying the impression of a cross-shaped plan. The use of free standing columns is a *leitmotiv* of Bolognese architecture during the modern age, when designers appreciated the monumental character of this solution. Stucco decoration and sculptures were realised by Angelo Piò with the help of Antonio Borelli and Giovanni Callegari. Mural paintings of the chapel of the Virgin were commissioned to Vittorio Maria Bigari and Claudio Ferroni.
ee906e22-472a-58c7-bafa-8ad9e8d52d69.location: Santuario della Beata Vergine di san Luca
ee906e22-472a-58c7-bafa-8ad9e8d52d69.artist: Carlo Francesco Dotti; Angelo Piò; Antonio Borelli; Giovanni Callegari; Vittorio Maria Bigari; Claudio Ferroni

ee9947e9-d8a3-563b-bf75-08af587efa7d.name: Martyrdom of Saint Peter and Saint Paul
ee9947e9-d8a3-563b-bf75-08af587efa7d.description: The church’s circular main fresco impressively illustrates the lives of its two patrons, St. Peter and St. Paul, in front of a surrounding architectural backdrop. The fresco displays a subtle colourfulness in a surreal stylization. With dramatic clarity, Günther depicts the martyrdom of the two apostles along the periphery of the fresco with Heaven looking on from the centre. The flat dome, which gives the illusion of being voluminous, is flanked by four pendentives, each of them containing an image of one of the four evangelists.

eea8e4f8-9634-582d-b793-e4253daa1b61.name: *Our Lady of Snow with Donors*
eea8e4f8-9634-582d-b793-e4253daa1b61.description: In the painted medallion are the kneeling figures of Adam Najšić, the chief notary of the Banovina of Croatia, and his wife, both of whom were donors of the church. Above them, on a cloud, sits Mary of the Snow with Christ on her lap. Below her, in the centre of the composition created as a skilful *trompe**\-**l'œil*, is the Roman Church of Santa Maria Maggiore in outline.
eea8e4f8-9634-582d-b793-e4253daa1b61.location: Ceiling, Parish Church of Our Lady of the Snow

f2c3e5c1-e11f-5d98-af35-9b30d507c062.name: High altar
f2c3e5c1-e11f-5d98-af35-9b30d507c062.description: The high altar includes a picture of the Saviour (*Salvatore*) given blessing in Laterano, near Rome, where the original is to be found. In front of the high altar are two tombstones covering the entrance to an underground crypt. The right one commemorates F. M. Šubíř of Chobyně founder of the church, the left one his wife and children. On a side altar to the left is a glass coffin containing the remnants of St. Felician, a martyr from the period of the first Christians, which was acquired in 1735. On the right is an altar of tools of the Lord's martyrdom with a replica of the Turin Shroud. The ceiling painting is modern.
f2c3e5c1-e11f-5d98-af35-9b30d507c062.location: Interior, Pilgrimage Church of the Elevation of the Holy Cross, Jaroměřice u Jevíčka

f3472803-8a49-5d58-b72d-b03b7f910c1b.name: “Amtshof” or the Ceremonial Courtyard
f3472803-8a49-5d58-b72d-b03b7f910c1b.description: In 1719 a fire destroyed the chateau interiors. Reconstruction was undertaken by C. A. Oedtl, who unified the chateau complex with a single frontage. He also rebuilt several other houses in the town. A ballroom was converted into a winter riding hall, and the theatre hall was reconstructed into a library; a *sala terrena* with a terrace was added and the ceremonial courtyard was refurbished, lined with busts of ancient emperors, and further decorated with *putti* and ornamental vases. The wrought-iron gates by H. G. Forster are original.
f3472803-8a49-5d58-b72d-b03b7f910c1b.artist: Christian Alexander Oedtl (1654 Paznaun – 1731 Vienna), Ignaz Lengelacher (1698 Unter Peissenberg – 1780 Baden), Heinrich Gottfried Forster

f4f82fea-ac97-5110-bd7d-d89aa7791475.name: Plan of the chateau and garden
f4f82fea-ac97-5110-bd7d-d89aa7791475.description: In 1650 Jan Rottal was appointed Imperial Secret Councillor. He was also the Supreme War Commissioner, Supreme Provincial Judge of Moravia and the Episcopal Court, Supreme Administrator of Orphans' Property, Chairman of the Royal Tribunal and Provincial Governor! Unsurprisingly, he maintained very close contacts with the court in Vienna. Luchese, in imperial service, made his reputation as a hydrological civil engineer. In Holešov, he designed broad canals along the flower parterre and divided it into four sections. These were adjoined by a kitchen garden and an orchard. The layout of the garden, in its time considered the most beautiful in Moravia, matched that of the chateau.

f5580fad-17e7-50ed-b62a-e9bc0f688102.name: View to the sanctuary
f5580fad-17e7-50ed-b62a-e9bc0f688102.location: Votive church of St. Mary of Jerusalem, Trški Vrh, near Krapina
f5580fad-17e7-50ed-b62a-e9bc0f688102.artist: Architect: Josef Hoffer (1700–1764); builder: Josip Javornik (active c. 1750); painter: Anton Joseph (Jožef) Lerchinger (Lerhinger) (c. 1720–after 1787)

f59127bb-d24a-50dc-95ab-b32b7ebbe922.name: Pilgrimage Altar (High Altar)
f59127bb-d24a-50dc-95ab-b32b7ebbe922.description: The two-storey pilgrimage altar, here designed due to the concept of a deeply staggered baldachino architecture, is a type commonly used in Bavaria for pilgrimages. In addition to the altar of mercy at ground level, it contains at gallery level a further celebration altar with an altarpiece that shows the Holy Family. The doughy moulded pedestals and entablatures stand in deliberate contrast to the faked marble materials.
f59127bb-d24a-50dc-95ab-b32b7ebbe922.artist: Altar Architecture: Dominikus Zimmermann (1685–1766) Sculptures: Ägid Verhelst (1696–1749) Altarpiece: Balthasar Augustin Albrecht (1687–1765)

f63aef53-1a4f-5d5f-b041-51c0d6fd9736.name: *Annunciation and Transportation of the Holy House*
f63aef53-1a4f-5d5f-b041-51c0d6fd9736.description:
Signed: *XTOFORO TASCA, 1714*  
The inscription beneath the painting reads *Munificentia Ilustrissimi Dni, Dni Francisci Ignatii Lib. Bar. de Androcha, Dni in Kostell., Kruppa etc. Haec Imago in honorem Miraculosissimae Virginis Tersactanae erecta fuit”; “Virgo sanCtIssIMa, HVIC BENEFACTORI NVnC IN artICVLO VLTae sVae, aC PERPEtVo Tva PIETaTE TVIsqVe GRATIIS PROPITIARE*. (By efforts of the noble Francis Ignatius Androcha, the baron of Androhia, the lord of Kostell, Kruppa etc. this image was painted in honour of the miraculous virgin of Trsat …)
f63aef53-1a4f-5d5f-b041-51c0d6fd9736.location: Triumphal Arch, Franciscan Church and Monastery of Our Lady of Trsat

f644b45d-6304-57e5-a71b-e23ab0fa362c.name: Archangel Raphael
f644b45d-6304-57e5-a71b-e23ab0fa362c.description: The railing opens, fan-like, onto the bridgehead, where the entrance is guarded by two angels on either side. Raphael accompanying little Tobias is, apart from St. Anne teaching the Virgin Mary, the only statue group on the bridge. The angel personifies the guardian spirit believed to accompany pilgrims and travellers. His name means “God heals” and he is identified with the angel who rippled the waters of Lake Bethesda, on the banks of which the diseased used to lie. The water of the lake was believed to have miraculous healing properties.

f8e1ad0b-17de-5672-8ca1-f12a32ae2481.name: Altar of St. Anthony (High Altar)
f8e1ad0b-17de-5672-8ca1-f12a32ae2481.description: With its Late Baroque shapes, the high altar contrasts strongly with the coloured side altars as it is fully gold-plated, a rare occurrence in Bavaria. In its centre, it bears a precious altarpiece. With a clear design and subdued colours, it depicts one of the main visions of the church patron: the blessed embrace of the Christ child. The imported art piece from Venice is characteristic for the market town of Partenkirchen as it is located near an important transit route in the Alps.

f97c18af-c344-543d-9c05-9aae43476c0f.name: Interior
f97c18af-c344-543d-9c05-9aae43476c0f.description: The space was planned by Hagenauer as a longitudinal building with a uniform sequence of four dome bays. Hueber reduced this to three, the central of which he configured as the main space above a quadratic ground plan with bevelled corner piers. Layers of pilasters and bold projecting cornices are further echoes of the Late Baroque. A sharp contrast is established by the ceiling stucco from Peter Plauder in true Early Classicist style executed in a highly two-dimensional manner, as does the austere composition of the high altar and pulpit, virtually devoid of ornamentation.
f97c18af-c344-543d-9c05-9aae43476c0f.artist: Wolfgang Hagenauer (1726–1801), Andrä Hueber [n.d.]; Peter Pflauder (1733–1811)

fa0f2509-a770-50de-bf2a-adc4110e9d91.name: Main Altarpiece
fa0f2509-a770-50de-bf2a-adc4110e9d91.description: The Main altarpiece is decorated with gilded wood carving in the Rococo style, similar to that of Tibães Monastery, although adapted to a narrower space. The entire structure is elevated. Five steps lead up to the throne occupied by the image of Our Lady that is under a baldachin.
fa0f2509-a770-50de-bf2a-adc4110e9d91.location: Church Interior, Chancel, Sanctuary of Our Lady of Good Remedy
fa0f2509-a770-50de-bf2a-adc4110e9d91.artist: Frei José de Santo António Ferreira (act.1764–66), Luís Manuel da Silva (act.1766)

fa7c0328-2962-5882-b92a-503ddeb0baf9.name: High altar
fa7c0328-2962-5882-b92a-503ddeb0baf9.description: Fontana, who was acquainted with Bernini’s work, made the rich figurative and decorative components give way to an image of the Virgin Mary Adored. The baldachin is topped with a sculpture of God the Father. Through the interplay of light and colour, and the transition of altar architecture into the stucco decoration of the vault, the baldachin accentuates the centrepiece of this pilgrimage complex.
fa7c0328-2962-5882-b92a-503ddeb0baf9.artist: Baldassare Fontana (1661–1733, Chiasso), Johannes Spillenberger (1628 Košice – 1679 Engelhartszell), Johann Hagenmüller, Bernard Antonio Fossati, Mikuláš Indegrenz

fb69020a-86ca-5884-8fbe-a4756b55b391.name: St. Fidelius of Sigmaringen
fb69020a-86ca-5884-8fbe-a4756b55b391.description: This picture of St. Fidelius of Sigmaringen was first painted by Kracker for the Capuchin Monastery in Znojmo. Sandrart lived in the monastery before being summoned to work for the Bishop of Jager. The Brno piece was probably an unfinished painting by J. T. Rotter in whose workshop Kracker worked after graduating from the Vienna Academy.
fb69020a-86ca-5884-8fbe-a4756b55b391.location: Capuchin Monastery and the Church of the Invention of the Holy Cross, Brno

fc8fe75f-aa42-5aa6-8958-3321f68494d9.name: Frontage
fc8fe75f-aa42-5aa6-8958-3321f68494d9.description: The convex-concave frontage traces the ground plan. The blind central entrance is particularly remarkable certainly holding symbolic meaning and probably embodying the third gate of St. John’s Revelation. Stone coats of arms of the church’s founder and his wife appear above the staircase, while a central cartouche features the bull of Pope Clement XI. Ledges that sit above crosses in shallow niches may symbolise Christ’s crown of thorns.
fc8fe75f-aa42-5aa6-8958-3321f68494d9.location: Pilgrimage Church of the Elevation of the Holy Cross, Jaroměřice u Jevíčka
fc8fe75f-aa42-5aa6-8958-3321f68494d9.artist: František Benedikt Klíčník? (1677 Ivanovice na Hané – 1755 Brno)

fcc7b9d9-0238-5ac6-acff-da0ef5f94db3.name: High altar
fcc7b9d9-0238-5ac6-acff-da0ef5f94db3.description: The austere Classicist high altar, flanked by double columns, was executed by Pflauder according to the design of Hagenauer and Nesselthaler. In contrast, Schöpf’s masterfully executed altarpiece depicting The Assumption of Mary with its Baroque contrasts of light and shade and wealth of figures radiates calm in respect of both composition and expressive content.
fcc7b9d9-0238-5ac6-acff-da0ef5f94db3.artist: Wolfgang Hagenauer (1726–1801); Peter Pflauder (1733–1811); Joseph Schöpf (1745–1822), Andreas Nesselthaler (1748–1821)

ff582151-3b73-57fb-86ef-7b3ab9f3c119.name: St. Joachim
ff582151-3b73-57fb-86ef-7b3ab9f3c119.description: This larger-than-life statue which is made still more impressive by emotional gesture and facial expression, is further enhanced by a spiral movement of the body with the lower part emphasised. St. Joachim, father of the Virgin Mary, holds in his right hand a dove brought as a sacrifice to the temple in Jerusalem. Sketches for the statues of Archangel Michael, St. Andrew and St. Joachim have been preserved in the collections of the Moravian Gallery in Brno; only slight modifications were made in the final execution.
